NATIONAL SAMPLE SURVEY
1103: SHRI VIJAYKUMAR HANSDAK:
Will the Minister of HEALTH & FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the findings of the recent 80th Round of National Sample Survey on Health and
the Economic Survey 2025-26 regarding the overall state of public health, morbidity rates and
out-of-pocket expenditure in India;
(b) whether the survey highlights a significant epidemiological shift from infectious diseases
towards non-communicable lifestyle illnesses such as diabetes and hypertension and if so, the
details thereof along with the steps being taken by the Government to address the issue;
(c) the details of the financial allocation and expansion targets achieved under the Ayushman
Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) and the inclusion of senior citizens under
Ayushman Bharat Vaya Vandana Scheme, in the country, State/UT-wise;
(d) the total number of functional Ayushman Bharat Health and Wellness Centres and Pradhan
Mantri Bharatiya Janaushadhi Kendras operationalised across the country to provide affordable
medicines; and
(e) the details of the policy measures and digital infrastructure upgrades, including the Ayushman
Bharat Digital Mission, to ensure universal, high-quality and affordable healthcare under the
"Health for All" roadmap?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH & FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI JAGAT PRAKASH NADDA)
(a) & (b): The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) conducted the latest
Survey on Household Social Consumption: Health during January 2025 to December 2025 as part
of the National Sample Survey (NSS) 80th Round. The report was released on 20.04.2026 and is
available on the Ministry's website. The key findings of the survey are enclosed at Annexure-I.
The findings of the NSS 80th Round are also consistent with the observations made in the
Economic Survey 2025-26, prepared annually by the Ministry of Finance, which notes that India
is undergoing an epidemiological transition. As per the NSS 80th Round report, the prevalence of
reported infectious diseases has declined between 2017-18 and 2025, whereas reported chronic
and non-communicable diseases (NCDs) have increased significantly during the same period.

Over the past few decades, India has witnessed a substantial decline in mortality from infectious
diseases and a rise in life expectancy at birth from 49.7 years in 1970-75 to 70.6 years in 2020-24.
The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare provides technical and financial support to States and
Union Territories across the country under the National Programme for Prevention and Control of
Non Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD) as part of the National Health Mission (NHM). The
programme focuses on strengthening infrastructure, human resource development, screening, early
diagnosis, referral, treatment, and health promotion for Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs).
Under NP-NCD, 770 District NCD Clinics, 233 Cardiac Care Units and 6,410 NCD clinics at
Community Health Centres have been set up across the country.
A population-based initiative for the prevention, control and screening of common non
communicable diseases (NCDs) i.e. diabetes, hypertension, oral, breast and cervical cancer, has
been rolled out across the country. Under the initiative, persons more than 30 years of age are
targeted for their screening and management at Ayushman Arogya Mandir.
(c) to (e): Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), a flagship scheme of
the Government of India, was launched on 23rd September 2018 to provide free and cashless
healthcare services to economically vulnerable families.
This scheme provides health coverage of Rs. 5 lakhs per family per year for secondary and tertiary
care hospitalization to 12 Crore families constituting bottom 40% of India’s population.
Additionally, in March 2024, around 37 lakh families of Accredited Social Health Activists
(ASHA), Anganwadi Workers (AWW) and Anganwadi Helpers (AWH) were included under the
scheme. In October 2024, the scheme was further expanded to cover 6 crore senior citizens of age
70 years and above belonging to 4.5 crore families irrespective of their socio-economic status. As
on 30th June 2026, a total of 44.19 crore Ayushman cards have been created under the scheme,
including 1.26 crore Ayushman Vay Vandana Cards for senior citizens aged 70 years and above.
The State/UT wise details Ayushman Cards created under AB PM-JAY and Ayushmann Vay
Vandana can be accessed at https://dashboard.nha.gov.in/public/card
A total amount of Rs. 39,837.52 crore has been released to States/UTs under AB PM-JAYsince its
inception. The State/UT wise fund released under the AB PM-JAY is attached as Annexure-II.

(b) As per the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) study published in 2025, states that the
socio-economic changes have influenced dietary patterns, leading to greater dietary diversity, but also
contributing to the rise of chronic diseases like cancer, cardiovascular diseases, and diabetes. Also the
evolution in the traditional diet over the years changed the diet patterns, which is perceived to be the
significant contributor to the increase in Non-Communicable Diseases (NCD) in the region as well as

(c) & (d) The Department of Health and Family Welfare provides technical and financial support to

Control of Non Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD) as part of the National Health Mission (NHM).

early diagnosis, referral, treatment, and health promotion for Non- Communicable Diseases (NCDs)
Under NP-NCD, 770 District NCD Clinics, 233 Cardiac Care Units and 6,410 NCD clinics at

ESSENTIAL MEDICINES IN CENTRAL GOVERNMENT HOSPITALS
1107. ADV .PRIYASAROJ:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the details of the availability of essential medicines in Central Government hospitals in
the country during the last five years, year-wise and State-wise, particularly in Uttar
Pradesh;
(b) whether there are any instances of stock-outs being reported for such medicines, if so,
the reasons for shortages of such medicines as identified in the Ministry reviews, if so,
the details thereof;
(c) the number of grievances received by the Government regarding the non-availability of
medicines and out-of-pocket expenditure incurred by patients across the country, State-
wise, particularly in Uttar Pradesh;
(d) the key findings of inspections and monitoring reports regarding procurement and
supply chain management of such medicines; and
(e) the corrective measures introduced by the Government relating to procurement, supply
and monitoring to ensure the uninterrupted availability of essential medicines in the
country?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND
FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (e): ‘Public health and Hospitals’ are the state subject. However, under the National
Health Mission (NHM), financial & technical support is provided to the States/UTs for
strengthening their healthcare delivery system including support for provision of free
essential medicines in public health facilities based on the requirements posed by States/UTs
in their Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs) within their overall resource envelope.
Under Free Drugs Service Initiative (FDSI), Government of India supports
procurement of drugs and strengthening robust systems of procurement, Quality Assurance,

Supply chain management and warehousing, Prescription audit, grievance redressal,
dissemination of Standard Treatment Guidelines and Establishment of IT enabled platform
DVDMS (Drugs & Vaccine Distribution Management System) for monitoring the real status
of procurement and availability of essential medicines.
Ministry of Health and Welfare (MoHFW) has recommended facility-type wise
Essential Medicines List (EML) to be made available at the public healthcare facilities which
includes provision of a variety of free medicines related to diseases. The facility-type wise
number of medicines in the EML includes 113 drugs at Sub Health Centre level, 179 at
Primary Health Centre level, 301 at Community Health Centre level, 318 at Sub-district
Hospital level and 381 drugs at district Hospital level. However, States have the flexibility to
add more medicines. Quality of drugs procured must be ensured by States/UTs.
The government has rolled out the Drugs & Vaccine Distribution Management
System (DVDMS), an IT-enabled platform to monitor the procurement status and ensure the
availability of essential medicines across the public healthcare system in real-time.
Government conducts regular review meetings with States/UTs to address operational gaps,
ensure maintenance of adequate buffer stocks, and strengthen grievance redressal
mechanisms.
The Central Government Hospitals follow the General Financial Rules, 2017 (GFR
2017), Manual for Procurement of Goods and other extant guidelines / instructions issued by
the Government of India as amended from time to time for the procurement of medicines.
The quality and uninterrupted supply of medicines in States/UTs is regularly
monitored by the Ministry through various review mechanisms, including Common Review
Missions (CRMs), Programme Review Meetings, field visits and inspections conducted by
Centre and State/UTs authorities.

entries.t: Service Condition  of AWWs and AWHs
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF WOMEN & CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1109 
ANSWERED ON 24.07.2026 
  
SERVICE CONDITION OF AWWs AND AWHs 
  
 
1109. SHRI KALI CHARAN MUNDA: 
 
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has received representations for enhancement of service 
conditions of Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) and Anganwadi Helpers (AWHs) from 
various States including Jharkhand, if so, the details thereof; 
  
(b)  whether the Government has examined the demand for implementation of gratuity for 
AWWs and AWHs in compliance with the directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, if so, 
the present status thereof; and 
  
(c)  the steps taken by the Government to improve their honorarium, social security benefits 
and service conditions? 
  
 
ANSWER 
 
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (c) Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) and Anganwadi Helpers (AWHs) are honorary workers 
drawn from the local community who voluntarily come forward to render their services in the area 
of child care and development to help the local community for which they are paid honorarium. 
This honorarium is increased from time to time. From 1st October, 2018, Government of India has 
enhanced the honorarium of AWWs at Anganwadi centres (AWCs) from Rs.3,000/- to Rs.4,500/- 
per month and AWHs from Rs.1,500/- to Rs.2,250/- per month as per the defined cost sharing ratio 
between the Centre and States and UTs. In addition, States and UTs are also paying additional 
monetary incentives and top ups to these functionaries from their own resources which vary from 
State to State. Details of additional top ups provided by States and UTs are at Annexure. 

Besides, performance linked incentive of Rs.500/- per month is provided to AWWs and Rs.250/- 
per month to AWHs. 
Under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, AWWs have been technologically 
empowered with the provision of smartphones for efficient monitoring and delivery of services. 
Poshan Tracker which is a mobile phone application that has digitized physical reg isters used by 
Anganwadi workers. This improves the quality of their work while simultaneously enabling them 
for real-time monitoring of all activities going on in the Anganwadis.   
To incentivize and encourage the AWWs and AWHs, various initiatives have been undertaken 
including the following: 
i. Promotion: Under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, promotional 
opportunities for AWWs and AWHs have been enhanced. 50% posts of AWWs are to be 
filled by AWHs with 5 years of experience and 50% posts of Supervisors are to be filled 
by promotion of AWWs with 5 years of experience subject to fulfilment of other criteria. 
ii. Leave: 20 days’ annual leave and paid maternity absence of 180 days and paid absence on 
abortion/ miscarriage once for 45 days. 
iii. State Governments and UT Administrations have been requested to encourage eligible 
AWWs and AWHs to get  themselves enrolled under the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi 
Mandhan (PM -SYM) Pension Scheme, which is a voluntary and contributory pension 
scheme for the unorganized sector in the country to ensure old age protection. 
iv. Social Security Insurance Schemes: Insurance benefits have been provided to AWWs and 
AWHs under Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) for life cover worth 
Rs.2.00 lakh (covers life risk, death due to any reason) in the age group of 18 to 50 year s 
and under Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana for accidental cover of Rs.2.00 Lakh 
(accidental death and permanent full disability) /Rs.1.00 Lakh (partial but permanent 
disability) in the age group of 18-59 years. 
v. Retirement date: States and UTs have been requested to adopt a uniform retirement date 
i.e 30 th April of each year with respect to AWWs and AWHs to ensure proper human 
resource planning. 
vi. Annual Healthcare coverage of Rs. 5 Lakhs under Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan 
Arogya Yojana (AB -PMJAY) to all AWWs and AWHs in pursuance to budget 
announcement in FY 2024-25.  
  
Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 is a centrally sponsored scheme and is implemented 
by the States/UTs. The Central Government is responsible for policy and planning and the State 
Governments are responsible for day -to-day program implementation and all operational aspects 

of the scheme. The Government of India releases funds in the prescribed cost -sharing ratio to the 
States/UTs for implementation of the Scheme. 
Since the implementation of the Scheme is done by the State Government/UT Administration 
therefore, no specific guidelines have been laid by the Government of India with respect to 
recruitment, retirement benefits, and payment of Gratuity for Anganwadi Workers and Anganwadi

entries.t: Standard of Foreign Medical Graduate Examination
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENTOF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1112
TO BE ANSWERED ON 24TH JULY,2026
STANDARD OF FOREIGN MEDICAL GRADUATE EXAMINATION
1112. SMT. SANJNA JATA V:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government is aware of the fact that Foreign Medical Graduate Examination
(FMGE) exams are meant for the students who have done their MBBS from a foreign soil to get
themselves registered in India and such exam is a mandatory screening/exam, if so, the details
thereof;
(b) whether it is a fact that despite being a screening/exam for MBBS graduates, the National
Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) has maintained the standard of FMGE
paper of NEET PG level which is least required for screening and in the latest FMGE exam
held
in June 2026, even questions of United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE) style
pattern appeared, thus putting the students under huge mental pressure, if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the Government is contemplating to request the concerned NBEMS to check their
standard of paper and to lower the qualifying exam marks to 125 rather than 150 marks for this
exam of June 2026 in view of the overall pass percentage for the NBEMS June 2026, exam
being just 12 per cent; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI JAGAT PRAKASH NADDA)
(a) to (d): The Foreign Medical Graduate Examination (FMGE) is conducted by the National
Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) in accordance with the provisions of
the Screening Test Regulations for Foreign Medical Graduates (FMGs) seeking provisional or
permanent registration with the National Medical Commission (NMC) or the respective State
Medical Councils (SMCs).
As informed by NBEMS, the questions for FMGE are developed through structured Question
Banking and Item Writing workshops followed by Validation Workshops by a different group
of subject experts. Each question is reviewed for content accuracy, relevance to the approved

syllabus, reliability and validity. The overall process ensures that the examination maintains
the expected standards of MBBS graduate and assesses the knowledge and competence
required for safe medical practice in the Indian healthcare system.
The FMGE is conducted strictly in accordance with the notified regulations and prescribed
qualifying criteria.
*****

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 1114 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 24.07.2026 
  
  
Skill Development through Anganwadi 
  
+ 1114 SHRI GYANESHWAR PATIL: 
            SMT. DELKAR KALABEN MOHANBHAI: 
 
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)       the steps taken by the Government to strengthen nutrition, health monitoring, and 
Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) under Mission POSHAN-2.0 and Saksham 
Anganwadi; State-wise including Madhya Pradesh and Dadra and Nagar Haveli; 
  
(b)       the details of the modernization (digital monitoring and smart infrastructure) of 
Anganwadi centres carried out by the Government in the State of Madhya Pradesh and 
Dadra and Nagar Haveli during the last three years and till date; 
  
(c)       whether the Government proposes to launch skill development and 
entrepreneurship programmes for women through Anganwadis and Self -Help Groups 
(SHGs) in Madhya Pradesh and Dadra and Nagar Haveli, if so, the details thereof; and  
  
(d)       the time-frame by which the Government proposes to implement the same? 
  
  
ANSWER 
  
  
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR) 
  
  

(a):      The Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 provides the following package 
of services in an integrated manner to eligible beneficiaries through a network of around 
14 lakh Anganwadi Centres (AWCs) spread all over the country:  
i. Supplementary nutrition. 
ii. Pre-school non-formal education. 
iii. Nutrition and health education. 
iv. Immunization. 
v. Health check-up. 
vi. Referral services. 
  
Three of the six services, viz., immunization, health check -up and referral services, are 
related to health and are provided through National Health Mission (NHM) and Public 
Health Infrastructure. 
  
Under Mission Poshan 2.0, a new strategy has been adopted for reduction in 
malnutrition and for improved health, wellness and immunity of children. It includes 
approaches like community engagement, outreach, behavioural change and advocacy. It 
focuses on Maternal Nutrition, Infant and Young Child Feeding Norms, treatment of 
Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM)/ Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) and wellness 
through AYUSH practices to reduce prevalence of wasting, stunting, anemia and being 
underweight. 
  
Supplementary Nutrition is provided to Pregnant Women, Lactating Mothers, 
Children (6 months to 6 years), and Adolescent Girls (in Aspirational Districts and North 
Eastern Region) in accordance with the nutrition norms contained in Schedule -II of the 
National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013. These norms have been revised in January 
2023. Revised norms are more comprehensive and balanced in terms of both quantity 
and quality of supplementary nutrition. It is based on the principles of diet diversity that 
provides for quality protein, healthy fats and micronutrients (Calcium, Zinc, Iron, Dietary 
Folate, Vitamin A, Vitamin -B6 and Vitamin B -12). Extra Supplementary Nutrition is 
provided to SAM children. 
  

For improving the quality of Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) delivered 
through Anganwadi system, Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi (PBPB) initiative was launched in 
May 2023 under the Mission. PBPB aims at equipping AWCs with high -quality 
infrastructure, play equipment, and well -trained Anganwadi Workers (AWWs).   Around 
11.44 AWWs have been trained in ECCE pedagogy and delivery of nutritional services in 
First Round of the training under PBPB. Under PBPB, allocation for Pre-school Education 
(PSE) Kits has been increased to ₹3,000 per AWC per year for providing adequate PS E 
kits at the AWCs. In order to improve the quality of ECCE, Navchetana - a National 
Framework for Early Childhood Stimulation for children up to 3 years of age, and 
Aadharshila - National Curriculum for ECCE for children of 3 to 6 years of age were 
launched in March 2024. Navchetana framework empowers caregivers and AWWs for 
holistic early stimulation of children through responsive caregiving. Aadharshila improves 
the quality of  early childhood education transacted at AWCs by prioritizing play -based 
activities covering all learning domains. 
  
Government has also approved upgradation of 2,00,000 AWCs to Saksham 
Anganwadi Centres  across the country except Delhi and Dadra and Nagar Haveli for 
better delivery of nutrition and increased focus on ECCE services to the beneficiaries. In 
Madhya Pradesh, numbers of AWCs sanctioned for upgradation as Saksham 
Anganwadis in 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 are as under: 
  
2022-23 2023-24 2024-25 
2,220 9,486 12,956 
  
  
(b):      In order to leverage Information Technology to strengthen and bring about 
transparency in nutrition delivery support systems at the AWCs, Government launched 
‘Poshan Tracker’ e-Governance portal having reach to all AWWs in the country including 
those of Madhya Pradesh and Dadra

support for ASHA workers lies with the respective State/UT Governments, as Health is a State
subject. Under National Health Mission (NHM), the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

healthcare system, based on the requirements posted by States/UTs in their Programme
Implementation Plans (PIPs) and within the overall resource envelope.
ASHAs receive incentive for routine and recurring activities. Additionally, they are provided
performance-based incentives for a varied set of activities under various National Health
Programmes. Incentives under ASHA program are revised regularly based on national priority

https://nhm.gov.in/New-Update-2025-26/ASHA-incentive/ASHA%20Incentives.pdf

Budget to supplement the amount received under NHM.
After the launch of Ayushman Arogya Mandir, ASHAs are eligible additionally for Team Based

entries.head:

IMPLEMENTATIONOF AB-PMJAYIN PUNE
1117. DR. AMOL RAMSING KOLHE:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the implementation of the Ayushman
Bharat–Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) in Pune District, Maharashtra and
the extent of coverage achieved among eligible beneficiaries, if so, the details thereof;
(b) the number of Ayushman cards issued, hospital admissions, claims submitted and claims
settled in Pune during the last three years and the current year;
(c) the details of public and private hospitals empanelled under AB-PMJAY in Pune and the
steps taken by the Government to expand the empanelled hospital network and improve
access to cashless treatment;
(d) whether any awareness campaigns and outreach programmes have been undertaken by the
Government to increase enrollment and utilization of the scheme among eligible beneficiaries
in Pune; and
(e) the measures being taken by the Government to ensure timely claim settlement, seamless
digital authorisation and uninterrupted cashless treatment under AB-PMJAY in Pune district?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND
FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a): National Health Authority (NHA) regularly conducts review meetings with State Health
Agencies to monitor the implementation of Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya
Yojana (AB-PMJAY), review key performance indicators, identify implementation
challenges, and ensure effective implementation of the scheme. As on 30.06.2026, a total of
22.15 lakh Ayushman cards have been created in the Pune district.

(b): During 01.04.2023 to 30.06.2026 a total of 18.30 lakh Ayushman cards have been issued
whereas the number of hospital admissions were 3.34 lakh and claims settled were 2.43 lakh
in Pune district.
(c): As on 30.06.2026, a total of 353 hospitals are empanelled in Pune district, comprising
181 government hospitals and 172 private hospitals. The details of the empanelled hospitals
can be accessed at: https://hem.nha.gov.in/search
Under AB-PMJAY ,hospital empanelment is a continuous process and is undertaken by the
implementing State/UT based on the requirements and availability of healthcare providers
meeting the criteria within a given State/UT as per empanelment guidelines of National
Health Authority (NHA). As on 30.06.2026, a total of 37,413 hospitals have been empanelled
under the scheme across the country, including 17,265 private hospitals. Further, to enhance
the participation of healthcare providers, particularly in rural and underserved areas, NHA
regularly reviews the status of hospital empanelment with State Health Agencies (SHA),
conducts sensitization meetings with hospitals and healthcare provider networks, and engages
with concerned stakeholders to facilitate the empanelment of eligible hospitals under the
scheme.
(d): NHA and SHAs have undertaken several measures in districts including Pune to improve
Ayushman card saturation, such as “Aapke Dwar Ayushman” campaign, door-to-door
mobilisation by frontline workers, and support through Common Service Centres etc.
The scheme has a comprehensive media and outreach strategy to spread awareness and
empower beneficiaries. This includes advertisement over various media platforms including
newspapers, community radio, street plays, digital displays, radio campaigns, mass
messaging, telecast of beneficiary testimonials etc.
(e): Under the scheme, settlement of claims is a regular and uninterrupted process and claims
are settled by respective SHAs as per claim adjudication guidelines issued by NHA. Further,
for timely settlement of claims, the permissible turnaround time is within 15 days of claim
submission for intra-state hospitals (hospitals located within the State) and within 30 days of
claim submission in case of portability claims (hospitals located outside the State).
The scheme is implemented through a robust end-to-end digital platform that enables timely
and efficient delivery of healthcare services. Further, Aadhaar-based authentication is
mandatory at the time of availing treatment to enable transparent, secure, and digital
authorization of healthcare services.

entries.t: Shortage of Fertilizers in Uttar Pradesh
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS 
DEPARTMENT OF FERTILIZERS 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1118 TO BE ANSWERED ON: 24.07.2026 
 
Shortage of Fertilizers in Uttar Pradesh 
 
1118   Shri Anand Bhadauria: 
          
Will the Minister of Chemicals and Fertilizers be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware of the widespread acute shortage of 
fertilizers, particularly Urea, DAP, and NPK, being faced by farmers across the 
country; 
 
(b)  if so, the details thereof along with the reasons for such acute shortage, State-
wise and fertilizer-wise; 
 
(c)  the quantum of fertilizers available to meet the demands thereof during the 
kharif season, State-wise and fertilizer-wise; and 
 
(d)  the measures taken by the Government to address the distress of farmers who 
are unable to get timely and adequate supplies of fertilizers, leading to delayed 
sowing and potential yield losses across the country, State-wise particularly in 
Uttar Pradesh? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS & FERTILIZERS 
 
(SHRI JAGAT PRAKASH NADDA) 
 
(a) to (d) Following measures are taken by the Government every season for 
ensuring adequate and timely availability of fertilizers to the farmers in the country: 
i. Before the commencement of each cropping season, Department of Agriculture and 
Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in consultation with all the State Governments, assesses 
the State-wise & month-wise requirement of fertilizers.  
 

-2- 
ii. On the basis of requirement projected by DA&FW, D/o Fertilizers allocates adequate 
quantities of fertilizers to States by issuing monthly supply plan and continuously 
monitors the availability.  
iii. The movement of all major subsidized fertilizers is monitored throughout the country 
by an on-line web-based monitoring system called integrated Fertilizer Management 
System (iFMS). 
iv. Regular Weekly Video Conference is conducted jointly by DA&FW and D/o 
Fertilizers with State Agriculture Officials and corrective actions are taken to dispatch 
fertilizers as indicated by the State Governments. 
v. The distribution of fertilizers within the State at district/ block level is done by the 
concerned State Government. 
In view of above, the availability of all the fertilizers viz. Urea, DAP, MOP and NPKS, 
has remained adequate across the States, including the State of Uttar Pradesh, during 
the ongoing Kharif 2026 season. The information regarding requirement, availability, 
sales and closing stock of these fertilizers in the States during the period 01.04.2026 
to 21.07.2026 is placed at Annexure. 
 
Further, State government of Uttar Pradesh has informed that no shortage of fertilizers 
has been observed in the State during the ongoing Kharif season and adequate 
quantities of all major fertilizers are being supplied continuously to farmers across the 
State.

entries.t: Poor Healthcare Facility at Bitra Island
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENTOF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1119
TO BE ANSWERED ON 24TH JULY,2026
POOR HEALTHCARE FACILITY AT BITRA ISLAND
1119. SHRI MUHAMMED HAMDULLAH SAYEED:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government is aware that the existing First Aid Centre at Bitra Island,
Lakshadweep, is inadequate to meet the healthcare needs of the Island's residents due to the absence
of a full-fledged Primary Health Centre (PHC), if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether the Government has received any proposal from the Lakshadweep Administration
for the upgradation of the First Aid Centre at Bitra into a full-fledged PHC with adequate medical
personnel, essential medicines, diagnostic facilities and emergency care services to ensure better
healthcare delivery for the residents of the Island; and
(c) if so, the details and the current status of the proposal, along with the timeline fixed for the same?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) to (c) : As per the Health Dynamics of India (Infrastructure & Human Resources) 2023-24,
the Union Territory of Lakshadweep has 4 Primary Health Centres (PHCs) in position.
Health being a state subject, the primary responsibility to strengthen healthcare facilities in
the State/UTs lies with the respective State/UTs. Under the National Health Mission (NHM), the
Government of India provides need based technical and financial support to the States/UTs,
including the UT of Lakshadweep, based on the proposals made by the States/UTs in their
Programme Implementation Plans (PIP) within their overall resource envelop duly approved by the
National Programme Coordination Committee (NPCC).
The UT Administration of Lakshadweep has not submitted any proposal for upgradation of
the existing First Aid Centre at the Bitra Island to the level of a Primary Health Centre in their
Programme Implementation Plan (PIP) for 2026-27.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LAW AND JUSTICE 
DEPARTMENT OF LEGAL AFFAIRS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1120 
TO BE ANSWERED ON FRIDAY, THE 24TH JULY, 2026 
  
RESERVATION LAW IN THE NINTH SCHEDULE OF THE CONSTITUTION 
  
1120.  SHRI E TUKARAM: 
  
Will the Minister of LAW AND JUSTICE be pleased to state: 
  
(a) whether the Union Government has received any request from the Government of Karnataka 
to include the State’s reservation law providing 56 per cent reservation for Scheduled Castes, 
Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution; 
 
(b) if so, the details of the request and the present status of its examination; 
  
(c) whether the Union Government proposes to introduce a Constitution Amendment Bill to 
include the said law in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution, keeping in view the request of 
the Government of Karnataka; and 
  
(d) if so, the likely timeline for introducing the Bill and if not, the reasons therefor? 
  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) OF THE MINISTRY OF LAW 
AND JUSTICE; AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS 
(SHRI ARJUN RAM MEGHWAL) 
(a) & (b): The Central Government had received a reference from the Government of Karnataka 
for inclusion of the Karnataka Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Reservation of Seats in 
Educational Institutions and of Appointments or Posts in the Services under the State) Act, 2022 
in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution. The Act, forming part of the State’s reservation 
framework, provides for 56 per cent reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and 
Other Backward Classes. The said Act, passed by the Karna taka State Legislature, has been

entries.t: POSHAN Tracker App
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
LOK SABHA 
  
Un-Starred Question no. 1121 
To be answered on 24.07.2026 
  
POSHAN Tracker App 
1121. Smt. Priyanka Gandhi Vadra: 
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has taken cognisance of reports of eligible pregnant women and 
lactating mothers and children being denied Take Home Ration (THR) under Saksham Anganwadi 
and POSHAN-2.0 due to errors in Facial Recognition system (FRS), Aadhaar e -KYC and OTP 
failures in the POSHAN Tracker App, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the details of eligible beneficiaries who have not received THR since FRS and OTP verification 
were mandated in July 2025, along with the reasons for such failures, State/UT-wise; 
(c) whether the Government is aware of the challenges faced by Anganwadi workers (AWWs) due 
to the additional digital tasks mandated under POSHAN Tracker App, if so, the details thereof and 
the action taken to address the same; and 
(d) whether measures are being taken to provide training and support to AWWs to enable the 
effective use of the POSHAN Tracker App, if so, the details thereof?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD 
DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR) 
  
(a) to (d) : Under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, the ‘Poshan Tracker’ digital 
application has been rolled out as an ICT based governance tool for monitoring and tracking of all 
activities in the Anganwadi Centres (AWCs), Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) and beneficiaries on 
defined indicators. It has facilitated mon itoring and tracking of near real time activities at nearly 
14 lakh AWCs in the whole country.  
To address network -related issues such as low or no internet connectivity in some areas while 
conducting e-KYC and Face matching under Facial Recognition System, (FRS) on Poshan Tracker 
for Take-Home Ration (THR) distribution, the application provides func tionality to conduct face 

matching in offline mode. OTP for e -KYC and Aadhar face matching has to be taken ONCE in 
entire life cycle of the beneficiary. It creates ease of living for the beneficiaries to avail the 
Anganwadi services even when network or server issues are present. For further ease of receiving 
benefits of THR, Nominee Module has been introduced in the application for Pregnant Women, 
Lactating Mothers, and Adolescent Girls. If due to any reason, the registered beneficiary is unable 
to visit the Anganwadi Centre to rec eive their THR through FRS, she can nominate a person on 
her behalf to receive her THR. 
As per Poshan Tracker data, e -KYC and face matching of the beneficiaries for THR distribution 
in the country has substantially increased in past one year from 70.82% in July 2025 to 97.87% in 
June 2026. State and UT wise details of e-KYC and Face matching (as of June 2026) is placed at 
Annexure. 
Due to digital reporting on Poshan Tracker rather manual data entry in 11 physical registers, 
workload and operational challenges of Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) have substantially been 
reduced. Reporting of daily activities like - opening of AWCs, daily attendance of children, 
distribution of THR and Hot Cooked Meal (HCM), activities conducted at AWC ( Pre-school 
education, Personal Hygiene sessions) etc. are also available in offline mode, independent of 
network availability.  This has become possible as the Poshan Tracker application has been 
specifically designed to allow data entry in offline mode and the data can get synced within 5 days 
of entry. The frontline functionaries i.e. Anganwadi Workers, Block Coordinators and Supervisors 
are equipped with smartphones to enter the data of services at Anganwadi Centres and programme 
monitoring in the field.  All AWWs are also provided funds for internet connectivity charges.  
The Ministry of Women and Child Development (MoWCD) provides continuous training and 
handholding support to AWWs for effective use of the Poshan Tracker application through the 
following mechanisms: 
• Learning videos and awareness documents: In the Resource section of the Poshan Tracker 
application, learning videos and awareness documents are available for AWWs which can 
be accessed by them at any point of time for effective delivery of their routine tasks. 
• Under the Poshan Bhi Padhai Bhi (PBPB) initiative, the MoWCD is imparting training to 
all the officials and field functionaries in the States and UTs through a cascading model of 
training, wherein Master Trainers (District Officers, Block Coordinators and Supervisors) 
are trained and the master trainers further train all Anganwadi Workers in the field. 
Training is imparted on different modules of Poshan Tracker, viz. Facial Recognition 
System (FRS), Geo -Tagging, Home Visit Scheduler etc. Block and District coordinators 
provide on-ground handholding support to AWWs and supervisors for effective usage of 
the Poshan Tracker Application and resolution of tec

entries.t: Use of Diabetes Drug Ozempic
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENTOF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1122
TO BE ANSWERED ON 24TH JULY,2026
USE OF DIABETES DRUG OZEMPIC
1122. SMT. KANIMOZHI KARUNANIDHI:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Government is aware of the growing use of certain GLP-1 class drugs, such
as Ozempic, which are approved for the treatment of diabetes, being increasingly used off-
label or without proper medical oversight, and the concerns raised regarding potential misuse
for non-diabetic purposes, if so, the details thereof; and
(b) whether the Government proposes to strengthen monitoring, prescription guidelines,
public awareness and vigilance mechanisms to prevent harm arising from inappropriate use
of such medications and if so, the details thereof?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYAPATEL)
(a): Drugs such as Ozempic, are required to comply with safety, quality and efficacy
requirements under the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019 prior to approval for
manufacture/import or marketing. Such approvals are granted by the Central Drugs Standard
Control Organisation (CDSCO) based on evaluation of clinical data and other scientific
evidence generated under the provisions of said rules.
CDSCO has approved GLP-1 receptor agonist drugs in India strictly for the
indications of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM) in adults and chronic weight management in
adults with specified medical conditions.
In view of the potential misuse by non-diabetes individuals, the prescription and use of
such drugs have been restricted exclusively to endocrinologists and internal medicine/
specialists. Initiation and continuation of therapy are required to be undertaken only under the
strict supervision and monitoring of the treating specialist physician. This regulatory
safeguard is intended to prevent inappropriate use and to ensure that these drugs are
administered strictly under qualified medical supervision, thereby mitigating risks associated
with misuse and unsafe consumption.

In addition, CDSCO has issued an Advisory dated 10.03.2026 to all concerned
stakeholders, emphasizing strict compliance with the provisions of the Drugs and Cosmetics
Act, 1940 and Rules made thereunder, and directing that manufacture, sale, and distribution
strictly conform to approved indications and conditions of permission.
(b): CDSCO has issued an advisory dated 27.03.2026 directing State/UT Drugs Controllers
to ensure strict adherence to the conditions of approval and the warnings specified on the
approved product labels for GLP-1 based weight loss drugs. It further emphasizes that the
manufacture/import, distribution, wholesale and retail sale and dispensing of such drugs shall
take place only through authorized channels and strictly in accordance with the approved
indications and labelling.
The advisory also directs the State/UT Drugs Controllers to initiate appropriate
regulatory action in cases involving diversion of products, leakage into unauthorized supply
channels, promotional practices influencing the supply chain, or any non-compliance with the
conditions of approval. In addition, they have been advised to undertake active monitoring of
print, electronic, digital, social media and outdoor advertising platforms to detect non-
compliant advertisements or surrogate promotional activities relating to these drugs.
Wherever violations are detected, appropriate action initiated under the provisions of
the Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act, 1954, the Drugs and
Cosmetics Act, 1940 and the Rules made thereunder against the manufacturers, importers,
marketers or any other entities.
Following steps has been taken by National Coordination Centre-Pharmacovigilance
Programme of India (NCC-PvPI), Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC), to strengthen
monitoring, public awareness to prevent harm arising from inappropriate use of GLP-
1 receptor agonists
(i). NCC-PvPI organized a meeting with representatives from Marketing Authorisation
Holders (MAHs) and Adverse Drug Reaction Monitoring Centers (AMCs) on
20th May, 2026 and 22nd March, 2026, respectively, to sensitize the stakeholders
about the safety of Semaglutide (Ozempic) and other GLP-1 receptor agonists and
reporting of suspected Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs) to the PvPI.
(ii). All AMCs under PvPI across the country have been sensitized through emails and
posters to closely monitor and report ADRs associated with semaglutide and
other GLP-1 receptor agonists.
(iii). Awareness posters have also been posted on IPC social media handles to encourage
healthcare professionals and the public to report ADRs associated with GLP-1 receptor
agonists including Semaglutide.
*******

entries.t: Implementation of POSHAN
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
LOK SABHA 
  
Unstarred Question no. 1124 
To be answered on 24.07.2026 
  
Implementation of POSHAN 
1124. Shri Sachithanantham R: 
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether despite the implementation of POSHAN Abhiyaan and other nutrition interventions, 
the National Family Health survey (NFHS-5) and subsequent Government data continue to show 
that over one -third of children under five are stunted and anaemia among  women and children 
remains very high; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has undertaken assessment of the reasons for these persistent 
outcomes along with the corrective measures proposed to achieve the nutrition targets; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof?  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD 
DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR) 
  
(a) to (d): Malnutrition is a complex and multi-dimensional issue, affected mainly by a number of 
generic factors including poverty, inadequate food consumption due to access and availability 
issues, poor maternal infant and child feeding and care practices, poor sanitary and environmental 
conditions, etc. As malnutrition requires a multi-sectoral approach involving dimensions of food, 
health, water, sanitation and education, it is crucial to effectively address the issue of malnutrition 
in a convergent manner. The issue is being addressed under the Mission Saksham Anganwadi and 
Poshan 2.0 (Mission Poshan 2.0) by establishing cross cutting convergence amongst more than 18 
Ministries/Departments. 
Further, various rounds of the National Family Health Survey (NFHS) conducted by Ministry of 
Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) have shown improvement in malnutrition indicators in 
children across the country. Details of these indicators for children since NFHS-1 to NFHS-6 are 
given below:

NFHS-2 (1998-99) ** 45.5 
NFHS-3 (2005-06) *** 48.0 
NFHS-4 (2015-16) *** 38.4 
NFHS-5 (2019-21) *** 35.5 
NFHS-6 (2023-24) *** 29.3 
Poshan Tracker Data of children measured in Anganwadi (June 2026) *** 29.30 
* Under 4 years              
** Under 3 years         
*** Under 5 years 
  
MoHFW also keeps record of data of children and women suffering from anaemia. As per NFHS-
5 (2019 -21) the prevalence of anaemia is 67.1 percent in children aged 6 -59 months and the 
prevalence of anaemia in women aged 15-49 years is 57 percent. 
As a whole of Government approach, high priority has been accorded to the issues of malnutrition 
in the country. Ministry of Women and Child Development (MoWCD), Ministry of Health and 
Family Welfare (MoHFW), Department of Food and Public Distribution (DFPD) and Department 
of School Education & Literacy (DoSE&L) are continuously undertaking targeted interventions to 
improve the health and nutritional status of children in the country. 
Mission Poshan 2.0 is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme under the  Ministry of Women and Child 
Development (MoWCD) to address the challenges of malnutrition in the country. The 
responsibility for implementation of various activities lies with the States and UTs.  Regular 
reviews are done by Ministry utilising the ‘Poshan Tracker’ digital application. It has facilitated 
monitoring and tracking of near real time activities at nearly 14 lakh AWCs in the country. The 
details are available at the link of   Poshan Tracker Public Dashboard: 
https://www.poshantracker.in/statistics. Also, review meetings of states and UTs are being done 
regularly through video conferencing. 
A third -party evaluation and impact assessment of Poshan Abhiyaan was conducted by NITI 
Aayog in 2020 and also in 2025 and has found its relevance to be satisfactory for tackling 
malnutrition in the country. 
  
Under Mission Poshan 2.0, various measures have taken by the MoWCD to improve nutritional 
outcomes: 
• Supplementary Nutrition is provided to Children (6 months to 6 years), Pregnant Women, 
Lactating Mothers and Adolescent Girls in accordance with the nutrition norms contained 
in Schedule -II of the National Food Security Act, 2013. Additional Nutrition is a lso 
provided to Severely Acute Malnourished (SAM) children in form of Take -Home Ration 
(THR). 

  
• One of the major activities undertaken is Community Mobilization and Awareness 
Advocacy in the form of Jan Andolans (Poshan Pakhwada and Poshan Maah -annually 
celebrated in the months of September and March -April, respectively) to educate people 
on nutritio nal aspects as adoption of good nutrition habit requires sustained efforts for 
behavioural change. 
  
• The ‘Poshan Tracker’ application has been rolled out as an important governance tool, 
facilitating dynamic identification of stunting, wasting, underweight prevalence among 
children. 
  
• To encourage diet-diversity and consumption of wholesome local produce, Poshan Vatikas

(f) whether there is a roadmap to double the foreign exchange earnings from AYUSH -based 
medical value travel by 2027 and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYUSH 
(SHRI PRATAPRAO JADHAV) 
(a) The Government introduced the Ayush Visa on 27 July 2023 to facilitate inte rnational 
visitors seeking Ayush-based treatment. The Ayush Visa (M-3) and Ayush Attendant Visa (M-4) 

Page 2 of 4 
 
are distinct sub -categories under the Medical Visa, enabling foreign nationals and  their 
attendants to avail Ayush  treatment in India. Details of the Ayush  visa obtained are provided in 
Annexure-I. 
(b) The Government has undertaken various initiatives to promote the Ayush Visa through social 
media, the official website and other outreach platforms across the country, including Madhya 
Pradesh. The Medical and Ayush Visa Portal, administered by the Ministry of Home Affairs 
(MHA), facilitates registration of eligible Ayush  hospitals and issuance of invitation letters for 
foreign patients. The Ministry of Ayush issued letters dated 20.05.2024 and 22.12.2025 to all 
States/UTs, including Madhya Pradesh, and other stakeholders for registration on the Portal. 
Further, the Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) issued by MHA were circulated to all 
concerned stakeholders for effective implementation of the Ayush Visa. 
(c) At present, no p roposal for establishment of Ayush  Wellness Hubs at all major international 
airports is under consideration in Ministry of Ayush. 
(d) National Accreditation Board for Hospitals and Healthcare Providers (NABH)  a constituent 
board of the Quality Council of India (QCI), is accredited by the International Society for 
Quality in Health Care (ISQua), a globally recognized organization that evaluates and accredits 
healthcare accreditation bodies. ISQua accreditation signifies that NABH's standards, assessment 
processes, and accreditation methodology are aligned with internationally accepted benchmarks 
for quality and patient safety in healthcare. 
(e) Ministry of Ayush does not provide any dedicated fiscal incentives exclusively to private 
healthcare providers for establishing world-class Ayush treatment centres. 
(f) The Government has adopted various measures to  promote Ayush -based Medical Value 
Travel (MVT) and strengthen India's position as a global destination for traditional medicine and 
wellness. These include the National Strategy and Roadmap for Medical and Wellness Tourism, 
introduction of the Ayush Visa (M -3) and Ayush Attendant Visa (M -4), implementation of the 
Central Sector Scheme for Promotion of Int ernational Cooperation for Ayush , promotion of 
NABH-accredited A yush hospitals and wellness centres, lau nch of the Ayush Quality Mark, 
operationalisation of Standard Treatment Guidelines (STGs), international academic 
collaborations and scholarships, establishment of the Ayurveda Training Accreditation Board 
(ATAB) and Yoga Certification Board (YCB), collaboration with the India Tourism 

Page 3 of 4 
 
Development Corporation ( ITDC), and organisation of Ayush -based Medical Value Travel 
Summits. However, the Ministry has not fixed any specific target to double the fore ign exchange 
earnings from Ayush-based Medical Value Travel by 2027.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF WOMEN & CHILD DEVELOPMENT  
  
 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION NO: 1126 
ANSWERED ON 24.07.2026 
 
 
ANGANWADI SERVICES IN HINGOLI 
 
 
1126.  SHRI AASHTIKAR PATIL NAGESH BAPURAO: 
 
Will the Minister of WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware that several villages in the tribal and rural areas of  
Hingoli Parliamentary Constituency are facing shortages of Anganwadi infrastructure, 
inadequate nutrition supply, vacancies of Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) and Helpers 
(AWHs) and insufficient facilities for pregnant women, lactating mothers and children, if 
so, the details thereof; 
 
(b)  the details of Anganwadi Centres (AWCs) sanctioned, operational and under construction 
in Hingoli district during the last five years, along with the number of vacant posts of 
AWWs, AWHs and Supervisors; 
 
(c)  whether the Government has conducted any assessment regarding malnutrition, anemia, 
school readiness and maternal and child health indicators in Hingoli district and if so, the 
findings thereof; and 
 
(d)  whether the Government proposes to establish additional AWCs, provide modern  
infrastructure, improve nutrition supply under Saksham Anganwadi and POSHAN-2.0 and 
fill all vacant posts in the district? 
  
  
ANSWER 
  
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRIMATI SAVITRI THAKUR) 
  

(a) to (d) Under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, a package of six services i.e 
Supplementary Nutrition (SNP), Pre-school Non-formal Education, Nutrition & Health Education, 
Immunization, Health Check-up, and Referral Services are provided to the eligible beneficiaries 
through Anganwadi Centres. Three of the six services, viz., Immunization, Health check -up and 
Referral Services are related to health and are provided through National Health Mission (NHM) 
& Public Health Infrastructure. These services are provided to the eligible registered beneficiaries 
i.e children up to the age of 6 years, Pregnant Women and Lactating Mothers across the country 
and Adolescent Girls in the age group of 14 to 18 years in Aspirational Districts of States and all 
districts of North Eastern Region through the platform of Anganw adi Centre. The district wise 
number of Anganwadi Centres (AWCs) is available at the link: 
https://www.poshantracker.in/statistics. 
Under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, various steps have been undertaken to 
improve the infrastructure facilities at Anganwadi Centres (AWCs). During 15th Finance 
Commission cycle, 40,000 Anganwadi Centres have been sanctioned for construction in  
convergence with MGNREGS. 
Further, States/UTs have also been advised to continue to tap funds for construction of AWC 
buildings from various schemes such as Member of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme 
(MPLADS), Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF), Finance Commission  Grants to 
Panchayati Raj Institutions, Multi - Sectoral Development Programme (MSDP) of Ministry of 
Minority Affairs, etc. 
Directions have been issued to States/UTs to co-locate Anganwadi Centres, which are running on 
rent without sufficient infrastructure, at nearby Primary Schools, where space is available. 
Guidelines for Co -locating Anganwadi Centres within Government Primary Schools have been 
issued jointly with Ministry of Education. 
Under PM-JANMAN (Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan), a total of 2,500 
Anganwadi Centres (AWCs) have  been sanctioned for construction in PVTG (Particularly 
Vulnerable Tribal Groups) areas out of which 178 AWCs has been sanctioned for establishment 
and construction in the state of Maharashtra including 20 AWCs in Hingoli Parliamentary 
Constituency. 
  
Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) launched by the Ministry of Tribal 
Affairs (MoTA ) focusses on convergence, outreach and saturation in approximately, 63,843 
villages. Under DAGJUA, 875 AWCs have been sanctioned for establishment and construction. 
Also, in order to improve the infrastructure facilities at AWCs, funds @Rs.17,000/- for providing 
drinking water facilities and @Rs.36,000/ - for construction of toilets are provided to States and 
UTs. 
Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 is a Centrally Sponsored scheme. The 
implementation of the scheme falls under the ambit of State Governments and UTs administration.

sustained engagements and video conferences so as to ensure uninterrupted delivery of services to

entries.t: Strengthening of Government Hospitals in Punjab
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENTOF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1129
TO BE ANSWERED ON 24.07.2026
STRENGTHENING OF GOVERNMENT HOSPITALS IN PUNJAB
1129. DR. DHARAMVIRA GANDHI:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Union Government is taking steps to strengthen Government hospitals in
Punjab on a priority basis and to ensure strict regulation and transparency in the
charges levied by private healthcare institutions, if so, the details thereof; and
(b) the details of the measures taken by the Government to regulate charges levied by
private healthcare institutions and strengthen Government hospitals in Punjab?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND
FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) & (b): Public Health & hospitals fall under the State list and therefore, the primary
responsibility of strengthening public healthcare system is with the State/UT. However, under
the National Health Mission, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare provides technical
and financial support to the States/UTs including State of Punjab to strengthen the public
healthcare system including strengthening of Government hospitals based on the proposals
received in the form of Programme Implementation Plans (PIPs) under National Health
Mission. Government of India provides approval for the proposal in the form of Record of
Proceedings (RoPs) as per norms & available resources.
To ensure availability of essential drugs and reduce the Out-of-Pocket Expenditure
(OOPE) of the patients visiting the public health facilities, Government has rolled out the
Free Drugs Service Initiative (FDSI) under National Health Mission. This includes financial
support to States/UTs for 113 drugs at Sub Health Centre level, 179 at Primary Health Centre

level, 301 at Community Health Centre level, 318 at Sub District Hospital level and 381
drugs at district Hospitals.
This Ministry supports ‘Free Diagnostics Service Initiative’ programme under NHM
with the aim to provide accessible and affordable pathological and radiological diagnostics
services closer to the community, which in turn reduces the Out-of-Pocket Expenditure
(OOPE). Diagnostics services are provided free of cost at all levels of public health facilities
(14 tests at Sub Centers, 63 at Primary Health Centers, 97 at Community Health Centres, 111
test at Sub District Hospitals and 134 tests at District Hospitals).
The Government of India, enacted ‘The Clinical Establishments (Registration and
Regulation) Act, 2010’ (CE Act) and notified ‘The Clinical Establishments (Central
Government) Rules, 2012’ thereunder to provide for registration and regulation of
Government as well as private clinical establishments belonging to recognized systems of
medicine i.e. Allopathy, Yoga, Naturopathy, Ayurveda, Homoeopathy, Siddha and Unani
System of medicines, or any other system of medicine as may be recognised by the Central
Government (except those of Armed Forces). The State Governments and Union Territories
Administration which have adopted the CE Act are primarily responsible for regulating their
hospitals including private hospitals as per provisions of the CE Act and Rules thereunder to
ensure the provision of affordable and quality healthcare to patients. As per the CE Act, all
the clinical establishments (Government & private) are required to fulfil the conditions of
minimum standards of facilities and services and inter-alia, display of rates charged by them
at a conspicuous place. The CE Act has empowered a registering authority at the District
level under the chairmanship of the District Collector / District Magistrate to take actions
including imposing penalties in respect of violation of its provisions.
****

Commission cycle, 40,000 Anganwadi Centres have been sanctioned for construction in 
convergence with MGNREGS. 
Further, States/UTs have also been advised to continue to tap funds for construction of AWC 
buildings from various schemes such as Member of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme 
(MPLADS), Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF), Finance Commission  Grants to 
Panchayati Raj Institutions, Multi - Sectoral Development Programme (MSDP) of Ministry of 
Minority Affairs, etc.

rent without sufficient infrastructure, at nearby Primary Schools, where space is available. 
Guidelines for Co -locating Anganwadi Centres within Government Prima ry Schools have been 
issued jointly with Ministry of Education. 
Various other initiatives have been undertaken for construction of AWCs under PM JANMAN 
and Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan for the targeted development of tribal population 
and VVP (Vibrant Village Programme) - Phase I, focusing on Northern border areas.

UTs.

reduction in malnutrition and for improved health, wellness and immunity through activities like 
community engagement, outreach, behavioural change and advocacy. It focus es on Maternal 
Nutrition, Infant and Young Child Feeding Norms, treatment of Severe Acute Malnutrition 
(SAM)/ Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) and wellness through AYUSH practices to reduce 
prevalence of wasting, stunting, anaemia and being underweight.

of the scheme on various parameters including health and nutrition status of the children and to 
make course corrections.

Centres for the expansion of Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy  (AYUSH) 
services in the Dumka Parliamentary Constituency during the last five years;

and other paramedical staff in these Institutions; and

Dumka Parliamentary Constituency, which has a large tribal population, for the expansion of  
AYUSH hospitals, integrated AYUSH health centres, cultivation of medicinal plants, yoga and  
naturopathy services and to enhance training and employment opportunities for the local youth?

THE MINISTER OF STATE (IC) OF THE MINISTRY OF AYUSH

implementation of different approved activities of SAAPs in different districts of Jharkhand 
including Dumka  Parliamentary Constituency as reported by State all has been utilised.

of doctors, pharmacists, yoga  instructors and other paramedical staff in AAM (Ayush) of 
Jharkhand including Dumka Parliament Constituency lies with the State Government. Further, as

promotion of Ayush system in Jharkhand including Dumka Parliament Constituency by providing

entries.t: Enrolment of Nurses and Midwives
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA
MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
DEPARTMENTOF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
LOK SABHA
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1138
TO BE ANSWERED ON 24TH JULY,2026
ENROLMENT OF NURSES AND MIDWIVES
1138: SHRI BENNY BEHANAN:
Will the Minister of HEALTHAND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the total number of registered nurses and midwives in the country, State/UT-wise;
(b) the number of nurses and midwives enrolled on the National Register Tracking
System(NRTS), State/UT-wise;
(c) whether the Government has assessed the impact of non-enrolment on verification of
credentials, inter-State mobility and workforce planning, if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the steps taken by the Government to increase enrolment and address technical and
procedural difficulties faced by nurses in registering in the NRTS?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH
AND FAMILYWELFARE
(SMT. ANUPRIYAPATEL)
(a) to (d): The State Nursing Councils (SNCs) as per the provisions of respective State Act
register nurses and midwives. SNCs maintain data base of available nursing personnel
practising in their States by registering various categories of Nurses and Midwives. As per the
records received from Indian Nursing Council (INC), there are 46.02 lakh nursing personnel
registered. State/UT-wise total number of registered nurses in the country is given at
Annexure I.
Nurses Registration & Tracking System (NRTS) is a fully computerised interactive
system launched by INC in association with the National Informatics Centre (NIC) for
maintaining a live register of nursing personnel. Nurses apply to get registered on NRTS and
after verification of their data by the concerned State Nursing Council, the nurse is issued a
Nurse Unique Identification Number (NUID) Card and Nurse Passbook. State/UT-wise total
number of enrolled nurses in the NRTS is given at Annexure II. For inter-state mobility
Nurses can apply to their respective Nursing Councils for NOC. NOC letter is sent via
email/hard copy to the requested council.
INC has conducted meetings with Registrars of State Nursing Councils to facilitate
implementation of NRTS. INC also conducts virtual training programmes, provides online
user manuals, and operates a dedicated helpdesk and technical support email for resolving
registration-related difficulties. This Ministry has also issued directions to State Governments
for implementation of NRTS.
*****

so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the Union Government is aware of severe regional disparities within Punjab's
health infrastructure such as lack of doctors, absence of trauma centres and step-motherly
treatment of entire districts such as Moga from health investments, if so, the details thereof;
and
(d) the steps taken by the Union Government to ensure that rural Punjab receives adequate
upgraged to primary health centre and community health centres to address health problems
in Punjab?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND
FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) and (b): In the State of Punjab, a total of 16.65 lakh families are eligible for health
coverage under Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY). State of
Punjab is implementing AB-PMJAY through a hybrid model, wherein claims up to Rs. 1 lakh
are settled through an insurance company, while claims exceeding Rs. 1 lakh and up to the
scheme limit are settled through the Trust mode.
AB-PMJAY is a centrally sponsored scheme, with the cost of implementation shared between
the Central and State Governments in the ratio of 60:40 for Punjab.

The funding of AB-PMJAY is entirely demand driven. National Health Authority releases
funds for scheme implementation to the States/UTs on the basis of utilization certificates for
previous releases and demand received from the States/UTs.
(c): Under Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS), ‘Establishment of new medical colleges
attached with existing district/referral hospitals’ with preference to underserved areas and
aspirational districts, where there is no existing Government or private medical college, 03
medical colleges have been approved in SAS Mohali, Kapurthala and Hoshiarpur for which
Rs. 223.40 crore has been released. Further, under the CSS for ‘Strengthening and
Upgradation of Govt. Medical Colleges for Increase of PG seats’, two colleges were
approved for increasing 87 PG seats for which Rs. 44 crore has been released by Central
Government.
Under the scheme for ‘Upgradation of existing State Government/Central Government
medical colleges to increase MBBS seats in the country’, 100 MBBS seats have been
approved in 02 colleges with an approved cost of Rs. 120 crore and entire central share of
Rs.72 crore has been released to the State Government.
Further, under National Programme for Prevention & Management of Trauma and Burn
Injuries, to reduce the incidence, mortality, morbidity, and long- term disabilities resulting
from accidents, five Trauma Care Facilities at Districts/Sub-District Hospital situated at
Pathankot, Jalandhar, Khanna, Fazailka and Ferozpur, in Punjab have been sanctioned.
(d): Under National Health Mission, through 1.86 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs in the
country, including 3,322 AAMs in Punjab, comprehensive primary healthcare is provided by
strengthening Sub Health Centres (SHCs) and Primary Health Centres (PHCs). These AAMs
provide preventive, promotive, rehabilitative and curative care for an expanded range of
services encompassing reproductive and child healthcare services, communicable diseases,
non-communicable diseases and other health issues.
The AAMs incrementally provide 12 package of primary health care services across the
country, encompassing reproductive and child care services, communicable diseases, non-
communicable diseases, palliative care and elderly care, care for common mental disorders,
neurological conditions (epilepsy, dementia) and substance use disorders management
(tobacco, alcohol, drugs), oral health, ENT care, and basic emergency care. Government of
India also initiated Ayushman Arogya Shivir, a monthly fixed day outreach programme to
create awareness among people at both SHCs and PHCs.
To complement the expanded services, the essential list of drugs & diagnostics has been
expanded to make available 179 drugs & 63 diagnostics at PHC-AAMs and 113 drugs & 14
diagnostics at SHC-AAMs.
Under the CSS component of Pradhan Mantri - Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure
Mission, support has been provided for the state of Punjab with provision of amount Rs.
755.65 crore for establishment of 22 Integrated Public Health Lab

AUTONOMOUS STATEMEDICAL COLLEGE
†1140. SHRI UTKARSH VERMA MADHUR:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the current status of the establishment of super-speciality wing such as Cardiology and
Neurology for the treatment of serious ailments at the Autonomous State Medical College (ASMC)
established in Lakhimpur-Kheri, Uttar Pradesh;
(b) whether the Government proposes to provide financial assistance to further strengthen the
infrastructure of this medical college by including it under the Union Government's Pradhan Mantri
Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (PMSSY), so that local patients do not have to be referred to Lucknow or

(c) the details of the block-wise progress of schemes being implemented to reduce the Maternal
Mortality Rate (MMR) and Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) in the Tharu dominated and remote areas of
Lakhimpur-Kheri situated along the Indo-Nepal border; and
(d) the details of the funds of amount of assistance provided by the Union Government to the district
under the National Vector Borne Disease Control Programme for the prevention of diseases like
encephalitis, dengue and malaria which spread every year in this Terai region?
ANSWER
THE MINISTER OF STATEIN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND FAMILYWELFARE
(SHRI PRATAPRAOJADHA V)
(a) & (b): Public Health and Hospital is a State Subject and the responsibility for strengthening of
healthcare system including human resource adequacy and service availability in the public health
facilities lies with respective State/UT Governments.
As per the information provided by the State Government of Uttar Pradesh, autonomous
State Medical College, Lakhimpur Kheri, has been established as per the norms and standards
prescribed by the National Medical Commission (NMC) for imparting undergraduate medical
education, with an annual intake capacity of 100 MBBS students. The college is presently equipped
with the departments, infrastructure, and facilities mandated under NMC regulations for MBBS
teaching. At present, Super-Specialty Departments such as Cardiology, Neurology, etc. have not been
established in the college. Serious patients related to ailments such as cardiology and neurology, etc.
are being treated by the faculties of the Department of General Medicine, and the patients requiring
super-specialist care are being referred to KGMU Lucknow/SGPGI.
(c): Under the National Health Mission (NHM), Government of India implements various schemes
to improve the maternal health services across all States and Union Territories, including Tharu

dominated and remote areas of Lakhimpur-Kheri situated along the Indo-Nepal border, including
Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY), Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK), Pradhan Mantri
Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA), Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan (SUMAN) and Monthly
Village Health, Sanitation and Nutrition Day (VHSND).
Additionally, Postnatal Care aims to strengthen the quality of post-natal care by laying
emphasis on detection of danger signs in mothers and incentivization of Accredited Social Health
Activists (ASHAs) for prompt detection, referral & treatment of such high-risk postpartum mothers.
Further, improvement of maternal health services is taken up by strengthening of infrastructure,
including functionalization of First Referral Units (FRUs), setting up of Maternal and Child Health
(MCH) Wings, operationalization of Obstetric High Dependency Units & Intensive Care Units (Obst.

The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) supports in implementation of
Reproductive, Newborn, Child, Adolescent Health and Nutrition (RMNCAH + N) strategy under
