entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1237 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
Ban on Single-Use Plastic 
 
1237.   SHRI ANIL YESHWANT DESAI: 
SHRI RAMVIR SINGH BIDHURI: 
SHRI SANJAY UTTAMRAO DESHMUKH: 
SHRI SANJAY HARIBHAU JADHAV: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware about the increasing level of pollution in cities due to 
various reasons; if so, the details thereof, Sources-wise; 
(b)  the standing of country in international index of pollution along with the steps taken by the 
Government to control the use of plastic and other polluting materials in the country; 
(c) whether the ban on plastic by the market is effective, if so the status of the ban on single-
use plastic bags across the country along with the data of prosecution against the violations of 
the rules including shop keepers and common consumers; 
(d) the reasons for open  and uninterrupted use of plastic in the national capital of Delhi in 
almost all the weekly markets along with the steps taken to check this practice; and 
(e) whether the Government has provided any financial or technical assistance to the States for 
the effective implementation of the Plastic Waste Management and if so, the details thereof, 
State-wise along with the details of any alternatives to plastic bags found by the Government 
or Non-Government Agencies? 
   
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
(a) to (e):  The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change notified Plastic Waste 
Management Amendment Rules, 2021, on 12th August 2021, prohibiting identified Single Use 
Plastic (SUP) items, which have low utility and high littering potential, with effect from 1 July 
2022. The notification also prohibits manufacture, import, stocking, distribution, sale and use 
of plastic carry bags having thickness less than one hundred and twenty microns with effect 
from 31 December 2022. Non-woven plastic carry bags of less than 60 gram per sqm (GSM) 
are also prohibited from 30th September 2021. 
 
States and Union Territories have been asked to undertake regular enforcement drives 
to implement ban on identified single use plastic items and on plastic carry bags having 

thickness less than one hundred twenty microns covering fruit and vegetable markets, 
wholesale markets, local markets, flower vendors, units manufacturing plastic carry bags etc. 
As per details provided by SPCBs/PCCs and details available at SUP compliance monitoring 
portal, a total of 8,62,356 inspections has been conducted, and 1990 tonnes of banned single 
use plastic items have been seized and a total of Rs. 19.85 crores of fine have been levied from 
July, 2022, till January, 2026. 
The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has also notified the Guidelines 
on the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) for plastic packaging vide Plastic Waste 
Management Amendment Rules, 2022, on 16th February, 2022. The Guidelines stipulate 
mandatory targets on EPR, recycling of plastic packaging waste, reuse of rigid plastic 
packaging and use of recycled plastic content. Under Swachh Bharat Mission Urban 2.0 (SBM-
U 2.0) implemented by Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and Swachh Bharat Mission 
(Grameen) phase II, implemented by Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, central 
assistance is provided to States/UTs for solid waste management including plastic waste 
management.  
Further, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC) prevents and 
control air and water pollution through enactment of Water (Prevention and Control of 
Pollution) Act, 1974, Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 and Environment 
(Protection) Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Central Pollution 
Control Board and State Pollution Control Boards/Pollution Control Committees undertake 
monitoring and enforcement activities as per mandate.  
 
To provide better air quality in urban areas, the Government has launched the National Clean 
Air Programme (NCAP) as a long-term, time-bound, national level strategy to address air 
pollution in 130 Non-Attainment and million plus cities/urban agglomerations in 24 States/UTs 
including North India. MoEFCC conducts Swachh Vayu Survekshan annually to rank 130 
cities, which are covered under National Clean Air Programme and the results are available on  
website of CPCB at https://prana.cpcb.gov.in/ncapServices/robust/fetchFilesFrom 
Drive/Swachh_Vayu_Survekshan_2025_Result.pdf.  Further, CPCB has formulated 
Comprehensive Environmental Pollution Index (CEPI), which is a rational number (ranging 
from 0 to 100) to characterize environmental quality at a given industrial area following

entries.head:
Page 1 of 2 
 
Government of India 
Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports 
Department of Sports 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1240 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
Development of Sports Infrastructure in Mathurapur 
 
1240. Shri Bapi Haldar: 
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of funds sanctioned and released under various Central 
sports infrastructure schemes for the State of West Bengal during the 
last three years and the current year, district-wise; 
 
(b) whether the Government  has received any proposal for development 
or upgradation of sports infrastructure, including stadiums, indoor halls 
and training facilities, in Mathurapur Lok Sabha Constituency and if so, 
the details and present status thereof; 
 
(c) whether the allocation for upgradation of sports infrastructure in 
West Bengal has increased during the last three years and the current 
year and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to strengthen grassroots sports 
infrastructure and identify sporting talent in Mathurapur and other 
coastal and rural areas of West Bengal? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS  
[ DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA ] 
 
(a) to (d)  ‘Sports’ being a State subject, the responsibility for 
development of sports, including development or upgradation of sports 
infrastructure, including stadiums, indoor halls and training facilities and 
identification of sporting talent , rests primarily with the respective 
State/Union Territory Governments. The Union Government supplements 
these efforts by bridging the critical gaps.  The Ministry of Youth Affairs 

Page 2 of 2 
 
and Sports implements the following schemes for the promotion of 
sports in the country, including in the State of West Bengal: 
 
(i)     Khelo India – National Programme for Development of Sports; 
(ii)     Assistance to National Sports Federations (NSFs); 
(iii) Cash Incentives to Medal Winners in International Sports Events 
and their Coaches; 
(iv) National Sports Awards; 
(v)     Pension to Meritorious Sportspersons; 
(vi) Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay National Welfare Prog ram for 
Sportspersons; 
(vii) National Sports Development Fund; 
(viii) Running Sports Training Centres through Sports Authority of 
India (SAI); and 
(ix) National Centre for Sports Science and Research (NCSSR). 
 
Details of the above schemes are available in the public domain on the 
websites of this Ministry and the Sports Authority of India. 
 
The Khelo India Scheme and National Sports Development Fund (NSDF), 
implemented by this Ministry, under which financial assistance for 
development of sports infrastructure is provided are  demand-driven 
schemes. The proposals received from the State/ Union Territory 
Governments and other eligible entities are considered for financial 
support, subject to their completeness, technical feasibility and 
availability of funds under the scheme. This Ministry has not received 
any proposal for development or upgradation of sports infrastructure, 
including stadiums, indoor halls and training facilities, in Mathurapur Lok 
Sabha Constituency . The details of the sports infrastructure projects 
approved an d their sanctioned cost, funds released and their physical 
and financial progress, under the Khelo India Scheme and National 
Sports Development Funds (NSDF), across the country, including in State 
of West Bengal, are available in public domain on the dashboards of the 
Ministry at https://mdsd.kheloindia.gov.in and 
http://www.nsdf.yas.gov.in/nsdf-glance.html, respectively.

(a)the number of States/UTs that have notified State -level Rules 
Matching the four consolidated Labour Codes as of date; 
(b)the details of the names of States/UTs yet to notify such rules; 
(c)the legal and enforcement status of the Codes in States that have 
not notified matching rules; and 
(d) the steps being taken by the Government to expedite uniform 
implementation across all States/UTs? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (d) The Government of India has implemented four Labour 
Codes, namely, the Code on Wages, 2019, the Industrial Relations 
Code, 2020, the Code on Social Security, 2020 and the Occupational 
Safety, Health and Working Conditions (OSH&WC) Code, 2020 with 
effect from 21 st November, 2025. The Central Rules under the said 
Labour Codes have been notified on 8th May, 2026. 
   Since ‘Labour’ falls under the concurrent subject, the 
States/UTs are also required to frame Rules under the Labour Codes. 
Most of the States/UTs have already taken measures and have 
finalised or published/pre -published the Rules under the Labour 
Codes. However, a few States/UTs are in the process of pre -
publishing/finalising the Rules. 
   Those provisions of the Codes which do not require any 
rule to be notified, are already in force. However, in the States, during 
the transition period, existing rules, regulations, notifications, 
standards and schemes under the repealed laws will continue to 
operate, in so far as they are not inconsistent with the provisions  of  
Contd..2/- 
 

:: 2 :: 
the new Labour Codes, ensuring continuity and avoiding any legal 
vacuum. 
  The Ministry of Labour and Employment is pursuing with 
stakeholders including States/UTs for expedited and uniform 
implementation of the Codes. In addition, several National and 
Regional Labour Conferences were held with States/UTs during 2025-
26 to discuss issues relating to four Labour Codes.

entries.t: Digitisation of Tulu and Coastal Kannada Manuscripts and Archives
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.1244 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
Digitisation of Tulu and Coastal Kannada Manuscripts and Archives 
 
1244. Shri Captain Brijesh Chowta: 
 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
a) whether the Government has reviewed digitisation of Tulu and Coastal Kannada manuscripts and 
archives and the proposals, institutions and locations covered in Dakshina Kannada; 
b) the details of funds sanctioned, released and utilised along with appraisal stage, beneficiaries, 
works and outputs, scheme-wise; 
c) the details of documentation, eligibility, conservation, capacity and State-level action gaps; and 
d) the details of the technical-assistance, appraisal and implementation timeline? 
 
 
   ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM 
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) During the National Manuscript Survey launched in March, 2026 under the Gyan Bharatam Mission 
(GBM), repositories in Dakshina Kannada district of Karnataka preserving manuscripts in Tulu, 
Kannada and Sanskrit have been identified. However, w.r.t. review of digitization of archives, National 
Archives of India (NAI) has informed that there is no such development. 
Based on the survey findings, eligible repositories having manuscripts, are considered for digitization in 
accordance with the Mission guidelines, subject to physical verification, institutional readiness and 
availability of resources. The digitization of eligible manuscript collections is a continuous process, 
executed after execution of the prescribed agreements, creation of metadata, quality assessment and 
compliance with the operational guidelines of GBM.  
 
(b) An allocation of Rs.60 crore has been made for the current financial year under GBM, out of which 
Rs.4.48 crore has already been utilized so far. The Mission provides project-based financial assistance to 
institutions holding manuscript collections to undertake activities relating to the identification, 
documentation, conservation, digitisation and publication of manuscript-based research works. It also 
supports capacity-building programmes for developing expertise in manuscriptology, conservation and 
digitisation. Financial assistance is considered on the basis of proposals received from institutions and 
their appraisal as per the prescribed procedures and guidelines of GBM. 
 

(c) Gyan Bharatam envisages the identification, documentation, conservation, digitisation, research, 
publication and dissemination of India's manuscript heritage irrespective of script, language, dialect, 
tradition, community or geographical location.  
Conservation interventions are undertaken based on the physical condition and specific requirements of 
manuscripts. The Mission also facilitates need-based capacity-building programmes to develop expertise 
among manuscript custodians and other stakeholders in areas such as manuscriptology, conservation and 
digitisation.  
The concerned State Governments and Union Territory Administrations have also been engaged to 
facilitate coordinated efforts and ensure comprehensive coverage of manuscript heritage across the 
country. 
 
(d) Technical assistance and institutional support are facilitated through the designated technology 
partners onboarded for various functions including metadata creation and its integration on National 
Digital Repository (NDR), deployment of equipments, AI-integrated digital platform and long-term data 
storage etc. Proposals received from eligible institutions are considered on case-to-case basis and in 
accordance with the applicable framework, operational requirements, availability of funds etc. and 
implementation is undertaken thereafter in a phased manner as per agreed terms and conditions.

entries.t: Factual Mistakes in Textbooks
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION AND LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 1245 
ANSWERED ON- 27/07/2026 
 
 
Factual Mistakes in Textbooks 
 
 
1245.   Shri Saptagiri Sankar Ulaka: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government is aware of reports regarding errors, factual inaccuracies and other 
mistakes in textbooks prescribed and distributed to students of Government schools in Odisha 
and if so, the details thereof, including the classes, subjects and textbooks affected; 
(b)  whether the Government has sought any report or clarification from the Government of Odisha 
regarding such errors and their impact on students and if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether the Government ha s examined if prescribed procedures for academic review, expert 
verification, proofreading and quality checks were followed before printing and distribution of 
such textbooks and if so, the findings thereof; and 
(d)  the steps taken/proposed to be taken by  the Government in coordination with the State 
Government to rectify or replace erroneous textbooks, fix responsibility for lapses and strengthen 
review and quality -control mechanisms to ensure that students receive accurate and error -free 
learning materials? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
 
(a) to  (d):  Education is in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and majority of the schools 
come under the purview of the respective State and UT Government.  The textbook development and 
distribution to students, comes under the domain of State/ UT Government. As informed by the State 
Government of Odisha, National Education Policy, 2020 has been implemented by the Govt. of 
Odisha from the year 2025 -26. Accordingly, 55 textbooks for Classes I to VIII were developed in 
alignment with NCERT Textbooks and distributed among the students for the academic session 2026-
27. Based on the feedback received from the public and the inhouse review of text books by the 
SCERT, a corrigendum on the errors found in different textbooks from Classes I to VIII was issued 
to all the DEOs, for use during the class room transaction.   
 
As p er information received from State, a  three-member Enquiry Committee, headed by the 
Development Commissioner -cum-Additional Chief Secretary, was constituted by the State 
Government to enquire into the matter of errors detected in the textbooks developed, p rinted and 
distributed to students of Class I to Class VIII.  Based on the report of the Committee, the State 
Government has taken corrective actions. Further the State Government has initiated necessary steps 
for providing error free text books to the students.

entries.t: Eco-Tourism Development and Community-based Conservation in Tamil Nadu
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TOURISM 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.1246 
ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
ECO-TOURISM DEVELOPMENT AND  
COMMUNITY-BASED CONSERVATION IN TAMIL NADU 
 
1246. THIRU D M KATHIR ANAND: 
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the status of eco-tourism initiatives supported by the Government in 
Tamil Nadu, including the Baralikadu eco -tourism project in the 
Karamadai Forest Range of Coimbatore district within the Nilgiri  
Biosphere landscape, where nature -based tourism activities are 
undertaken with participation of tribal communities; 
(b) the details of the initiatives implemented/proposed to be 
implemented for promoting eco -tourism models that combine 
conservation of forests, rivers and biodiversity with sustainable 
livelihood opportunities for tribal and forest-dwelling communities; 
(c) the details of the programmes undertaken for strengthening visitor 
facilities, interpretation centres, skill development, community 
participation and promotion of eco-tourism destinations across Tamil 
Nadu; 
(d) the details of funds allocated, released and utilised under eco -
tourism, sustainable tourism and community-based tourism schemes 
during the period from 2020-21 to 2025-26; and 
(e) the details of outcomes achieved in terms of tourist arrivals, local 
employment generation, conservation awareness and economic 
benefits to communities residing near protected and forest areas? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM           (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (e):  Development of tourist destinations and products including eco-
tourism is primarily undertaken by the respective State Government/Union 
Territory (UT) Administration. The Ministry complements the efforts of 
States/UTs through various schemes and initiatives. 
 

The Ministry of Tourism through its central sector schemes of 
‘Swadesh Darshan, ‘Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual, Heritage 
Augmentation Drive (PRASHAD) and ‘Assistance to Central Agencies for 
Tourism Infrastructure Development  ’extends financial assistance to the 
State Governments / UT Administrations for tourism infrastructure 
development in the country.  The central financial assistance is being 
extended according to guidelines and based on proposals / detailed project 
reports received from the States and UT Governments.  
 
The guidelines for ‘Challenge Based Destination Development’ has 
been formulated as a sub scheme of Swadesh Darshan 2.0 Scheme to 
enhance tourist experience and to transform tourist destinations as 
sustainable & responsible destinations. 
 
Under the above schemes, the Ministry considers sanctioning a range 
of components which may enhance tourism facilitation at the destinations, 
as per project requirement including those related to tourism core 
products, tourism activities, safety, sanitation, last mile connectivity,  
parking, general site development, soft interventions etc. 
 
The details of projects sanctioned in the State of Tamil Nadu are 
given at Annexure. 
 
With the aim to promote tourism in tribal areas, the Ministry of 
Tourism has issued guidelines along with template for formulation of 
proposal by State Governments and UT Administrations for 'Development 
of Homestays in Tribal Areas' (A sub-scheme of Swadesh Darshan Scheme) 
under Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya  Unnat Gram Abhiyan (PM -JUGA). The 
objective of the initiative is to develop homestays in tribal areas to promote 
responsible tourism and enhance livelihood opportunities for tribal 
communities. The guidelines also focus on technical upskilling and training 
of the Homestay owners. The said initiative includes development of 1000 
homestays with support of Up to ₹5 lakh for village community 
requirement, Up to ₹5 lakh for construction of two new rooms for each 
household and Up  to ₹3 lakh for renovation of existing rooms for each 
household. 
 
Various schemes, programs, and initiatives of the Ministry including 
Paryatan Mitra/Paryatan Didi, Hunar Se Rozgar Tak etc. have been actively 
addressing issues related to skill development, creation of awareness on 
economic benefits, sustainability etc. 
 

In order to provide impetus for development of eco -tourism in the 
country, Ministry of Tourism formulated National Strategies for eco -
tourism and Sustainable Tourism and initiated Travel for LiFE programme 
to promote sustainable tourism in the country and to encourage the 
tourists and tourism businesses to adopt sustainable tourism practices.

entries.t: Promotion of Global Tourism and Cultural Infrastructure in Uttar Pradesh
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1248 
ANSWERED ON 27/07/2026 
 
PROMOTION OF GLOBAL TOURISM AND CULTURAL INFRASTRUCTURE IN 
UTTAR PRADESH 
 
✝1248.SHRI TANUJ PUNIA: 
 
Will the Minister of Culture be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of the schemes currently being implemented by the Government to promote global 
tourism and strengthen cultural infrastructure in the major cultural and religious centres of Uttar 
Pradesh, such as Varanasi, Ayodhya, Mathura and Prayagraj; 
 
(b)whether the Government is considering any special package for the preservation of the 
endangered folkart forms of Uttar Pradesh, such as Nautanki, Charkula dance and 'Kajri Gayan' 
and for providing financial assistance to local artists;  
 
(c)whether if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d)the details of the funds allocated and released to Uttar Pradesh for the said purpose during the 
last two years? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM  
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (c)     Government of India promotes global tourism and strengthen cultural infrastructure 
in India including the major cultural and religious centres of Uttar Pradesh. The Ministry of 
Tourism provides Central Financial Assistance (CFA) to State Governments (including Uttar 
Pradesh) and Union Territory Administrations under Domestic Promotion and Publicity 
including Hospitality Scheme for organizing fairs, festivals, and tourism-related events.  
 
         Ministry of Culture promotes global tourism and strengthen cultural infrastructure in Uttar 
Pradesh through the different Schemes run by this Ministry and its Cultural Institutions. Under 

the Global Engagement Scheme, the Ministry has empanelled Artists/Groups under various art 
forms for performing in the Festival of India (FoIs) abroad. Currently, 627 Artists/Groups are 
empanelled with the Ministry. Out of which, 31 artists/groups are from Uttar Pradesh. 
 
          North Central Zone Cultural Centre with its registered office at Prayagraj provide facilities 
for creative development of arts and literature with special emphasis on folk and tribal arts in its 
Zone including the Uttar Pradesh.  Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA) has a 
regional centre at Varanasi which undertakes activities relating to the research, documentation, 
preservation and dissemination of India’s art and Culture heritage including the folk-art forms of 
Uttar Pradesh. National School of Drama supports the promotion and preservation of traditional 
and folk theatre forms, including those from Uttar Pradesh, through its training programmes, 
seminars, workshops, theatre productions and festivals, as part of its regular activities. Similarly, 
the Centre for Cultural Resources and Trailing (CCRT), implement various programmes to 
promote and preserve India’s cultural heritage that supports cultural tourism across the country 
including the Uttar Pradesh.  
           In addition, the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), an organization under the 
Ministry of External Affairs, provides performance opportunities to artists representing diverse 
traditional and folk-art forms of Uttar Pradesh through its monthly cultural programmes 
organized by Zonal Office in Lucknow across the state.  
          ICCR has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with State Government of Uttar 
Pradesh to promote their art and culture abroad.  ICCR sponsors India’s folk-art troupes 
including from the Uttar Pradesh to perform in different countries across the world and also 
sponsors participation of foreign cultural troupes/artists across the country including the Uttar 
Pradesh. During the last two years, ICCR has facilitated participation of over 200 international 
artists in several iconic cultural festivals/events hosted by the State Government of Uttar 
Pradesh.  
 
(d) No funds allocated and released specifically to Uttar Pradesh for the said purpose during 
the last two years.

entries.t: e-Waste Management
entries.head:
OIH 
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1249 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
  
e-Waste Management 
 
1249. DR. SAMBIT PATRA: 
  
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has launched any scheme for the management, disposal, and recycling 
of electronic waste (e-waste) and if so, the details thereof; 
(b) the number of cases of violation of the national e-waste policy that have come to light during the 
last three years along with the action taken in such cases, State/UT-wise; 
(c) the number of surprise inspections conducted by the Government to ensure compliance with the 
said policy during the last three years along with the action taken against the violators, State/UT-
wise; 
(d) whether cases of dumping of e-waste imported from foreign countries have also come to the notice 
of the Government and if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) the details of the policy formulated for the prevention of dumping of e-waste imported from 
foreign countries? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE 
CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (c)  Ministry has notified the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 in November, 2022 under 
the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 after comprehensive revision of the E-Waste (Management) 
Rules, 2016, and the same is in force since 1st April, 2023. These rules provide for managing e-waste 
in an environmentally sound manner and putting in place an improved Extended Producer 
Responsibility (EPR) regime for e-waste recycling wherein all the manufacturer, producer, 
refurbisher and recycler are required to register on portal developed by the Central Pollution Control 
Board (CPCB). These rules promote Circular Economy through EPR regime and scientific 
recycling/disposal of the e-waste.  
 
Under Rule 24 of the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, there is provision for verification and 
audit by the CPCB or through a designated agency, to verify compliance of these Rules through 
random inspection and periodic audit, as deemed appropriate, so as to take action against violations 
of these Rules. CPCB has developed an audit module in the E-Waste EPR portal for carrying out 
audit through mobile app and web application. CPCB has developed guidelines for levying 
Environmental Compensation (EC) under the rules and the same is available at E-waste EPR portal.  
CPCB has also issued direction on 03.07.2026 under Section 5 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 
1986, wherein, State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs)/ Pollution Control Committees (PCCs) have 
been directed to carry out audits of recyclers in phased manner. Further, under Schedule-V of the E-
Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, SPCBs/ PCCs have been given the responsibility to monitor 
compliance of EPR and conduct random inspection of recycler and refurbisher and monitoring 

recycling capacity utilization. Information on such violations is maintained by the respective 
SPCBs/PCCs.  
 
(d) & (e) The import and export of hazardous and other wastes is regulated under the Hazardous 
and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) (HOWM) Rules, 2016 notified by 
the Ministry, which provide a comprehensive framework for the transboundary movement of 
hazardous and other wastes in line with the provisions of the Basel Convention. The Rules 
categorically prohibit the import of hazardous and other wastes for the purpose of disposal in India. 
Further, e-waste falling under Basel No. A1180 (waste electrical and electronic assemblies or scrap) 
is listed in Schedule VI of HOWM Rules, 2016, and import of such e-waste is prohibited.  
 
*****

entries.t: Loans waived off in Dadra and Nagar Haveli
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF FINANCIAL SERVICES 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 1251 
 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY, 27 JULY, 2026/SHRAVANA 5, 1948 (SAKA) 
Loans waived off in Dadra and Nagar Haveli 
†1251. SMT. DELKAR KALABEN MOHANBHAI: 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:- 
(a) whether the Government has any record of total loans waived or written off in respect of 
corporates and farmers in various States of the country during the last two years and the 
current financial year; 
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise; 
(c) the details of such loan waivers/loans written off separately for corporates and farmers in  
the Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli; 
(d) whether the Government has made any comparative assessment of the impact of debt 
relief given to farmers vis -à-vis corporate debt write -offs in the context of public finance and  
economic equity; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (c): The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has apprised that the State/Union Territory (UT) - 
wise and sector -wise details  regarding total loans waived off or written off in respect of 
corporates and farmers is not maintained by it. However, year-wise and category-wise details of 
loans written -off by Public Sector Banks, Private Sector Banks, Foreign Banks and Small 
Finance Banks, for domestic operations, for categories Large (Industries & Services) and 
Agriculture & Allied Activities, during the last two financial years (FY), are at Annex. 
(d) and (e): Debt write-off is an accounting procedure and does not provide any relief to the 
debtor (whether farmer or corporate). As per RBI - Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions 
2025, issued for commercial banks, write -off (a major portion of which is due to 
technical/prudential/advances under collection) is an accounting procedure undertaken by a 
bank to cleanse the balance sheets of bad debts which are either considered unrecoverable or 
whose recovery is likely to consume disproportionate resources of the lenders. Such write -off 
does not result in waiver of liabilities of borrowers and therefore, it does not benefit the 
borrower. The borrowers continue to be liable for repayment and banks continue to pursue 
recovery actions initiated in these accounts.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMIC AFFAIRS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1254 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026/ Shravana 5, 1948 (Saka) 
STATUS OF PURVODAYA SCHEME 
+1254  Shri Dinesh Chandra Yadav:  
Shri Ramprit Mandal: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:  
(a) the present status of the Purvodaya Scheme for the all -round development of the eastern region of the 
country covering the States of Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh as announced in 
the Union Budget 2024-25; and 
(b) the assistance being provided to all the States covered under the said scheme along with the details 
thereof?  
  
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI. PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a)&(b):  In the Union Budget 2024-25, the Government announced to formulate a plan (not a scheme) titled 
as Purvodaya, for the all-round development of the eastern region of the country, covering Bihar, Jharkhand, 
West Bengal, Odisha, and Andhra Pradesh , to cover human resource develo pment, infrastructure, and 
generation of economic opportunities to make the region an engine to attain Viksit Bharat. Towards this, the 
NITI Aayog had constituted an Inter-Ministerial Advisory Committee, with representatives from the state 
governments of Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, and West Bengal, to prepare a roadmap for the 
development of the Purvodaya states . Accordingly, in the Union Budget 2026 -27, the Government has 
announced three major initiatives under the Purvodaya Plan: (i) development of an integrated East Coast 
Industrial Corridor with a node at Durgapur; (ii) creation of five tourism destinations in the Purvodaya States 
and (iii) provision of 4,000 e-buses. In addition, the Government has undertaken several other initiatives for 
the development of Purvodaya states in the previous Union Budgets since the announcement on Purvodaya, 
such as development of an industrial node at Gaya; development of road connectivity projects, namely Patna-
Purnea Expressway, Buxar-Bhagalpur Expressway, Bodhgaya, Rajgir, Vaishali and Darbhanga Spur; and 
power projects, including the setting up of a new 2400 MW power plant at Pirpainti . Additional measures 
include central assistance for the development of tourist destinations in Odisha ; Kopparthy Industrial Area 
in Andhra Pradesh under Vizag Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC); Polavaram Irrigation Project; Orvakal 
Industrial Area in Andhra Pradesh under Hyderabad Bengaluru Industrial Corridor (HBIC) ; grants for 
backward regions of Rayalaseema, Pra kasam and North Coastal Andhra; support to the mineral-rich states 
including Odisha and Andhra Pradesh to establish dedicated Rare Earth Corridors to promote mining, 
processing, research and manufacturing etc.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1255 
ANSWERED ON 27/07/2026 
 
Hostel Accommodation for OBC Students in Central Universities 
 
1255 Shri Rahul Gandhi: 
 
Will the Minister of Education be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the total number of students enrolled in each Central University, 
social category -wise, including the number of Other Backward Class (OBC) 
students; 
(b) the details of the total number of hostel seats avai lable along with the number of 
hostel seats reserved for OBC students in each Central University; 
(c) whether reservation for OBC students is implemented in the allotment of hostel 
accommodation in Central Universities, if so, the details thereof and if not, the 
reasons therefor; 
(d) the details of funds allocated during the last ten years for the provision of hostel 
accommodation to OBC students in Central Universities, year -wise, along with the 
hostel capacity created and expenditure incurred thereunder  and the number of 
students accommodated therein, social category-wise; and 
(e) whether the Government has conducted any assessment regarding the financial 
burden on students due to non -availability of hostel accommodation in Central 
Universities, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (e) Education is a subject in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and comes 
under the purview of both the Central and State Governments. 
At present, a total of 3,09,542 students are enrolled in 47 Central Universities. The 
details of hostels available in Central Universities and the number of students 
accommodated therein are enclosed at Annexure -1. Approximately 32% of the 
students residing in the hostels of Central Universities belong to the OBC category. 
All Central Universities are statutory autonomous organisations established under 
the respective Central Acts of Parliament and governed by their Acts, Statutes and 
Ordinances made thereunder. The Universities are competent to take administrative 
and academic decisions, including allotment of hostel accommodation, with the 
approval of their respective Statutory Bodies. 

 
With the increasing number of students, additional hostel infrastructure is being 
created by the Universities from time to time to meet students' accommodation 
requirements. The Central Government supports development of university 
infrastructure, including hostels, through Grant -in-Aid and funding from Higher 
Education Financi ng Agency (HEFA).  It may be noted that during FY 2013 -14, ₹ 
5603.79 crore was released as grant to Central Universities. From FY 2014 -15 to FY 
2025-26, ₹ 1,13,943.55 crore was released to Central Universities  (Annexure-2). 
During the year 2026 -27, an amount of ₹ 17,440 crore has been allocated.  These 
funds are utilized by the Universities for meeting their academic, administrative and 
infrastructural requirements in accordance with their priorities. 
The Union Budget 2026 –27 announced provision of Viabi lity Gap Funding 
(VGF)/capital support for girls' hostels in Higher Education Science, Technology, 
Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) institutions, covering every district. 
Further, the OBC Expansion Scheme was introduced to facilitate implementation of 
27% reservation for OBCs in Central Higher Educational Institutions through 
corresponding expansion of institutional capacity. The Scheme was implemented for 
a period of five years commencing from 2008 -09, with the utilisation period for non -
recurring/building grants subsequently extended up to 31.03.2019. Financial 
assistance was provided to 13 Central Universities under recurring and non-recurring 
heads. Under the OBC Expansion Scheme, an amount of ₹2,496.93 crore was 
released during 2008 -09 to 2018 -19 to 1 3 Central Universities . The grant releases 
were primarily concentrated during the implementation phase of the Scheme, with 
further releases made during the extended utilisation period. 
The Government is implementing different scholarship schemes for provid ing 
financial assistance to all categories of students including students belonging to the 
Other Backward Classes (OBC) and other weaker section, subject to extant scheme

component schemes namely, Post Matric Scholarship and Top -Class College

Classes (EBC) and DNT students to pursue higher education in the country; and 
Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme (SHREYAS -OBC)

entries.t: Transparency in Insurance Coverage and Home Loan Practices
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF FINANCIAL SERVICES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1257    
 
 ANSWERED ON MONDAY, JULY 27, 2026/ SHRAVANA 5, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
Transparency in Insurance Coverage and Home Loan Practices 
 
1257. SMT. SMITA UDAY WAGH: 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has undertaken any assessment regarding public awareness 
about the distinction between deposit insurance, life insurance and accident insurance linked 
to bank accounts, if so, the details thereof; 
(b) whether the Government proposes to strengthen disclosure norms to ensure that banks 
clearly inform customers about insurance coverage and voluntary enrolment under 
Government-backed insurance schemes, if so, the details thereof; 
c) whether the Government has reviewed the practice of banks and housing finance companies 
requiring borrowers to purchase investment products or maintain deposits while sanctioning 
home loans, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether any regulatory framework exists to prevent unfair cross-selling and ensure 
transparency in home loan sanction conditions, if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) whether the Government proposes to issue uniform guidelines to protect borrowers from 
misleading practices and strengthen consumer awareness in banking services and if so, the 
details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (e): National Centre for Financial Education (NCFE), an organization promoted by 
Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), Insurance 
Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) and Pension Fund Regulatory and 
Development Authority (PFRDA), is specifically formed to promote financial education across 
India for all sections of the population, and to create financial awareness and empowerment 
through campaigns, seminars, workshops, conclaves, training, discussion forums. Such 
campaigns are conducted with the help of financial institutions and other bodies, and include 
awareness about different financial products, including, inter alia, life insurance, accidental 
insurance and banking products. Further, Life Insurance Council and General Insurance 

Council have launched insurance awareness programmes across the country to create 
awareness about insurance products, including, inter alia, life insurance, health and accidental 
insurance. Public awareness is also promoted by Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee 
Fund (DICGC) about deposit insurance from time to time. 
Banks promote financial products and also create awareness about their features e.g. basic 
accidental death or permanent disability coverage provided free along with debit card, and 
voluntary government-backed insurance products, such as, Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima 
Yojana, Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana, etc. 
RBI has issued Master Directions regarding ‘Responsible Business Conduct’ and ‘Undertaking 
of Financial Services’ — with the focus on enhancing the level of customer service and ensuring 
fair conduct towards customers by banks, and to ensure uniformity in its guidelines to protect 
borrowers from misleading practices and strengthen customer awareness with respect to 
banking services. 
As per the directions issued by RBI, banks are required to ensure that its policies and practices 
do not create incentives for mis-selling of products / services, whether its own or offered on 
behalf of a third-party. Banks are also directed to not resort to compulsory bundling of any 
product, including, inter alia, investment products, insurance products and deposits, with any of 
its own product/service, including, inter alia, home loans. However, if the sale of the bank’s own 
product / service is contingent on purchase of a third-party product, including, inter alia, 
insurance products, as a risk mitigant, customers are required to be provided the option to 
purchase the said product from any third-party product/service provider. 
In order to prevent unfair mis-selling and promote transparency in banking services, including, 
inter alia, loan sanction conditions, RBI has directed banks to adopt a fair practice code and 
ensure that no incentive is directly or indirectly received by the bank’s employees from the third-
party product/service provider for sale / marketing of any third-party product/service. Further, 
banks are required to establish a mechanism to seek feedback from customers within a 
specified timeline to ensure that customers have understood the features of the financial 
product / service and also the risks associated with such financial product / service. Customers 
may also lodge complaint regarding mis-selling of a financial product / service with the bank 
within the timeline specified by the respective financial sector regulators. 
*****

entries.t: Training in Emerging Technologies
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1258 
ANSWERED ON  27/07/2026 
  
TRAINING IN EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES 
  
1258. SHRI ANUP SANJAY DHOTRE: 
  
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has undertaken any initiatives to impart training in emerging 
technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, Data Analytics, Cyber Security, Drone 
Technology and Green Skills during the last three years and the current year; 
 
(b)  the number of candidates particularly Akola district, who have benefited from such 
programmes from Maharashtra; 
 
(c)  whether the Government has collaborated with educational institutions, industry and 
technology partners to expand training in future-ready skills; 
 
(d)  whether there is any proposal to establish specialised training facilities for emerging 
technologies in Maharashtra, including the Vidarbha region; and 
 
(e)  if so, the details thereof along with the expected timeline for implementation? 
  
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP  
  
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
  
(a) & (b):  Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM), the Ministry of Skill 
Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up-skill training through an 
extensive network of skill development centres  under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri 
Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship 
Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training 
Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the society across the country including Maharashtra. The 
SIM aims at enabling the youth of India to get future-ready, equipped with industry-relevant skills. 
 
The new age/future skills job -roles aligned with Industry requirements in areas like Artificial 
Intelligence, Robotics, Data Analytics, Cyber Security, Drone Technology and Green Skills has 
been introduced in the long -term as well as short -term training programs. Details of the 
candidates trained in Maharashtra including its Akola district, in the job -roles pertaining to areas 
like Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, Data Analytics, Cyber Security, Drone Technology and Green 
Skills are given at Annexure-I. 
 
To enable skill development in the Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) 
sector, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology implemented two schemes, viz. (i ) 
“Scheme for Financial Assistance to select States/UTs for Skill Development in Electronics 
System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) Sector” and (ii) “Skill Development in ESDM for 
Digital India”. The schemes concluded on 30.08.2025. Under both the Schemes, 4,93,919 
candidates were enrolled/trained and 3,75,289 candidates have been certified.  
 
The National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology (NIELIT) through its wide 
network of own centres and Accredited Training Partners/Facilitation Centres, has trained more 

than 43 Lakh candidates in last 5 years under various Degree/Diploma Level Courses and Skill -
Based Courses (Long Term & Short Term), including the Digital Literacy & Cyber Security 
Programmes across the country. NIELIT has also launched the NIELIT Digital University (NDU) 
Platform under MeitY  to deliver online and blended skill -based courses in emerging technology 
areas. This Platform is designed to offer future -ready, industry -aligned programs in emerging 
technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Cloud Computing, and other frontier 
domains. This platform also features built -in virtual labs for real -time experimentation in 
Semiconductor Design, cybersecurity, Cyber Forensics, Industry 4.0, and other emerging 
domains. 
 
(c):  To ensure that the skills imparted are aligned with the industry requirements and to 
expand training in future -ready skills, the following specific steps have been taken by MSDE 
across the country including Maharashtra: 
 
• National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET) has been set up as an 
overarching regulator establishing regulations and standards to ensure quality in the 
Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) space. NCVET recognizes the 
industry bodies as the Awarding Bodies (ABs) and/or Assessment Agencies (AAs). 
• The Awarding Bodies are expected to develop the qualifications as per the industry 
demand and map them with the identified occupations as per the National Classification of

qualifications as per the industry requirements, out of which 2975 qualifications are valid 
and active, and 7234 qualifications are archived. Out of total, 678 qualifications are 
categorized as the future skills qualifications by NCVET.

entries.t: Museum Grant Scheme and Preservation of Cultural Heritage
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No. 1259 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27/07/2026 
 
“MUSEUM GRANT SCHEME AND PRESERVATION OF CULTURAL HERITAGE” 
 
1259. SHRI ANURAG SHARMA:  
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the Museum Grant Scheme being implemented by the Government for the 
establishment, modernization, expansion, digitization and conservation of museums 
across the country, including the eligibility criteria and funding pattern; 
(b) the details of proposals received, approved, and grants released under the scheme, along 
with the museums that have benefited during the last five years, State-wise;  
(c) whether the Government has taken any steps to encourage the development of museums 
in aspirational districts and historically significant regions, including those showcasing 
the legacy of freedom fighters, tribal communities and local heritage; 
(d) whether any proposals from Bundelkhand, particularly Jhansi, have been received or 
approved under the said scheme and if so, the details thereof; and  
(e) the details of the measures taken/being taken to promote digital museums, public 
participation, tourism and public-private partnerships for the preservation and promotion 
of India's rich cultural heritage? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM 
 
(GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) Ministry of Culture operates Museum Grant Scheme under which financial assistance is 
provided for setting up of New Museums/development of the existing 
museums/digitization of museum collections/setting up of virtual museums and training of 
museums professionals of museums managed by Central/State Governments, Societies, 
Autonomous bodies, Public sector Undertaking, local bodies, Academic Institutions and 
Trusts registered under the societies Act at the regional, State and District Level in the 
country.   

Eligibility Criteria: For the purpose of support under this component, museums have 
been classified into three categories as per the existing guidelines of the Museum Grant 
Scheme : 
 
(i) Category I: Central or State Government owned museums in State Capitals 
including Museums owned by Public Sector Undertakings. 
(ii) Category II: Central or State Govt. owned museums including Museums of Public 
Sector Undertakings 
(iii) Category III: All other museums including Museums of Public Sector 
Undertakings  
Category I : Existing renowned Museums of the Central or State Governments located in 
the state capitals, subject to the following:  
i) The museum must be located in the capital of the state/union territory. 
ii) It must be of high repute, having a significant collection of objects/artefacts. 
iii) It must have had an annual footfall of 1 lakh visitors per annum in the preceding 2 
years. 
Category II : Central or State Govt. owned museums including museums of PSU 
Category III: Projects of Societies, Autonomous bodies, local bodies, Public Sector 
Undertaking, Academic Institutions and Trusts registered as a society under the Indian 
Societies Act of 1860 (XXI) or a similar legislation of the state governments, or as a 
Public Trust under any law at the time being in force subject to the following: 
(i) It should have been in existence for at least three years prior to the application. 
However, this condition can be relaxed in exceptional cases at the discretion of 
the Expert Committee, the reasons for which should be recorded in writing;  
(ii) It should have a well-defined constitution and laid down rules/bye laws for its   
functioning 
(iii)  It should be in ownership and possession of a substantial collection of objects of 
historical and / or cultural importance for display in the museum.  
(iv) It should be able to maintain the Museum and bear all recurring costs; 
(v) It should have the necessary infrastructural facilities, resources and     personnel 
to execute the work for which the grant is required;  
(vi) It should produce a certificate from the State Government (Department of   
Culture or equivalent) attesting to its satisfactory performance;  
(vii) It should not be run for personal profit.  
(viii) It should be the owner of the land on which the museum is situated or proposed to 
be constructed, which should be easily accessible to visitors.   

 
Ministry of Culture, Government of India may take up   any project under Category I &II 
as project of National importance at its discretion for the purpose of development of 
Museum & Cultural Spaces.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION

ANSWERED ON 27/07/2026 
 
Quota for EWS Seats in Private Unaided Schools 
 
1260. Shri P C Mohan: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of seats reserved and filled under the 25 per cent quota for 
economically weaker sections in private unaided schools in Karnataka, including 
Bengaluru, during each of the last five years and whether this represents growth o r 
decline from the earlier average of about 1.5 lakh admissions annually; 
(b) the impact of Karnataka's 2018 amendment introducing the neighbourhood school 
exemption on RTE admissions in the State; 
(c) whether reimbursement of per-child cost to private schools in Karnataka under the 
Scheme is being released in a timely manner and the amount pending, if so, the 
details thereof; and 
(d) the steps being taken by the Central Government to ensure States including 
Karnataka do not dilute the RTE quota for underprivileged children? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
(a) to (d): The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 
mandates the appropriate Government to provide free and compulsory element ary 
education to every child of the age 6 to 14 years in a neighbourhood school. 
‘Education’ is in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and majority of schools are 
under the jurisdiction of the respective State Government and Union Territory 
Administration which are the appropriate Government for implementation of the 
provision of the RTE Act, 2009.  
Section 12(1)(c) of ‘The RTE Act , 2009  provides for admission of children 
belonging to weaker sections and disadvantaged groups in Class I (or below) in the  
schools specified in sub -clauses (iii) and (iv) of clause (n) of section 2 of the Act to 

the extent of at least 25 percent of the strength of that class. For implementation of 
the provision of the Act, the respective State Governments / UT Administrations notify 
the disadvantaged groups and weaker sections and per child cost as per the laid 
down procedure. Section 12(2) of the RTE Act, 2009 provides for reimbursement to 
the private unaided schools for admitting children under Section 12(1)(c) of the Act.  
The Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Samagra Shiksha, provides financial 
assistance to States and Union Territories for various activities/works including 
reimbursement of expenditure incurred for admissions made under Section 12(1)(c) 
of the Act, in accordance with the norms of the scheme.  
As per information provided by the State Government of Karnataka, the 
Karnataka Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (Amendment) Rules 
2018 were notified to provide that admission under Section 12(1)(c) would  be 
available only where there is no Government or aided school in the defined 
neighbourhood offering the relevant class.  
The reimbursement of per-child cost to private schools for students enrolled in 
all elementary classes under RTE Act in Karnataka is being released in a timely 
manner as informed by the State Government.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)   the details of funds released under the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme 
(NAPS) to establishments in Andhra Pradesh during 2024-25 and 2025-26, year-wise; 
 
(b)   the number of apprentices enrolled and stipend support disbursed under the NAPS in 
Andhra Pradesh during the said period, district-wise; 
 
(c)   whether the Government is aware that districts including Alluri Sitharama Raju, Bapatla, 
Konaseema and Parvathipuram Manyam recorded low or zero enrolments under the Scheme in 
the said years; and 
 
(d)   if so, the details thereof and the steps taken/being taken to engage industries and

ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP  
 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) was launched in August 2016. 
Thescheme was extended to continue as NAPS -2 from FY 2022 -23. Under, NAPS 2.0, the 
stipend support by Government of India (GoI) is paid through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to the

A total of Rs.41.69 crore (including Rs.40.30 crore DBT amount) released to the state of Andhra

(c) & (d) Apprenticeship engagement under the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme

The Apprentices Act, 1961 provides a framework for establishments to utilize their training 
infrastructure and workplace facilities for imparting apprenticeship training. Under the Act, 
establishments employing four or more workers are eligible to engage apprentices, while

through Regional Directorates of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (RDSDEs) and other

organized across the country since June 2022 to facilitate engagement between employers and

based on local requirements. Apprenticeship opportunities under NAPS are available across all 
districts, including Alluri Sitharama Raju, Bapatla, Konaseema and Parvathipuram Manyam,

participation of both establishments and youth in apprenticeship training.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
LOK SABHA

ANSWERED ON - 27/07/2026 
 
Implementation of University Townships and Education-to-Employment Initiatives 
 
1263.    Adv. Chandra Shekhar : 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the details of the criteria adopted for the selection of locations and the proposed timeline  
for the development of the five "University Townships" near major industrial and logistics 
corridors; 
(b) the details of the proposed composition, mandate, functions and present status of the High-
Powered Education-to-Employment and Enterprise Standing Committee; and 
(c) the details of the action taken by the Government to integrate Artificial Intelligence (AI) 
and Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming and Comics (A VGC) into school curriculum 
frameworks, along with the mechanism proposed to assess the impact of these initiatives 
on youth employability? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (c): The Government of India has framed and approved the National Education Policy 
(NEP) 2020 to transform the education landscape into a multidisciplinary, inclusive, and 
learner-centric ecosystem. It accords high priority to enhancing access, equity, and qual ity of 
education for everyone. It promotes provision of physical infrastructure, digital tools & 
connectivity, and greater industry-academic linkages. 
 
In line with the vision of NEP 2020, it has been announced in the Union Budget 2026-27 that 
the Union Government aims to support States through challenge route, in creating 5 University 
Townships in the vicinity of major industrial and logistic corridors. Department of Higher 
Education has initiated consultation process with relevant stakeholders such as Sta te 
Governments, Academia, Industry representatives etc.  
 
To make India a global leader in services, and to optimise the potential for growth, employment 
and exports, assessing the impact of  emerging technologies, including AI, on jobs and skill 
requirements and propose measures thereof, Union Budget 2026-27 has also announced setting 

up of a High -Powered ‘Education to Employment and Enterprise ’ Standing Committee to 
recommend measures that fo cus on the Services Sector as a core driver of Viksit Bharat. 
Composition of the Committee is at Annexure.  
In line with NEP 2020, the Central Board of Secondary Education ( CBSE) has integrated 
Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Computational Thinking (CT) into the school curriculum. The 
framework introduces AI from the preparatory stage to build AI -literate learners by 2030, 
focusing on computational thinking, digital literacy, innovation, problem -solving, and 
responsible technology use.  
To ensure availability of professionals for Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming and Comics 
(A VGC) Sector, Government of India has announced in Union Budget 2026-27 to set up A VGC 
Content Creator Labs in 15,000 secondary schools and 500 colleges  by supporting  Indian 
Institute of Creative Technologies, Mumbai.

entries.t: Assessment of the Quality of Forest Cover
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1264 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
 
Assessment of the Quality of Forest Cover 
 
 1264.  SHRI VARUN CHAUDHRY: 
            SHRI JAI PRAKASH: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether there is any proposal under consideration for providing access to better satellite resolution to 
Forest Survey of India for improving the accuracy of India State of Forest Report, if so, the time frame by 
which it will be accessible, if not, the reasons therefor; 
(b) whether the Government has undertaken an independent assessment of the quality of forest cover, 
including forest density and biodiversity, in addition to the area reported in the India State of Forest 
Report, if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the details of forest land diverted for non-forest purposes during the last three years, State/UT and 
sector-wise; and  
(d) whether compensatory afforestation has been carried out against all forest land diverted during the last 
five years, if so, the details of land identified, plantations raised and survival rates? 
  
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE 
CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH)  
(a) & (b) Forest Survey of India (FSI), Dehradun, an organization under the Ministry of Environment, 
Forest and Climate Change, carries out the assessment of forest and tree cover of the country biennially 
and publishes the findings in the India State of Forest Report (ISFR). The forest cover assessment is a 
wall-to-wall mapping exercise based on interpretation of multi-temporal satellite data supported by 
extensive ground truthing.  
FSI periodically adopts technological and methodological advancements for improving the accuracy and 
reliability of forest cover mapping. Over the years, these advancements have included the use of improved 
satellite data, mapping at higher scales, and refinement in image interpretation techniques, while ensuring 
consistency and comparability of the assessment over time.  
The ISFR provides an assessment of the quality of forest cover in addition to the extent of forest cover. 
The report classifies forest cover on the basis of canopy density into Very Dense Forest (canopy density 
of 70% and above), Moderately Dense Forest (canopy density of 40% to less than 70%) and Open Forest 
(canopy density of 10% to less than 40%). 
 
(c)  The details of forest land approved for diversion under the provisions of the Van (Sanrakshan Evam 
Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980 during the last three years, State/UT-wise and sector-wise, are given at 
Annexure-I and Annexure-II, respectively. 
(d)   In compliance of the conditions stipulated under the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) 
Adhiniyam, 1980, the compensatory afforestation is taken up by the concerned State/UT. As per  the 
reports received from the States/UTs, the compensatory afforestation over an area of 1,78,261.52 hectares 
has been carried out during the last five years. The survival percentage of these  plantations have been 
reported between 40% to 100%.

entries.t: Nutritional Standards under the PM POSHAN Scheme
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION AND LITERACY 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 1265 
ANSWERED ON- 27.07.2026 
 
Nutritional Standards under the PM POSHAN Scheme 
 
1265. Shri Abhishek Banerjee:  
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of States/Union Territory providing eggs under the PM POSHAN Scheme during the 
last five years, including the number of beneficiary children covered and the frequency  of egg 
supply, State/UT and year-wise; 
 
(b) whether the Government maintains data on States, districts or implementing agencies  where 
eggs have been withdrawn, reduced or replaced by vegetarian substitutes, if so, the reasons therefor 
and the number of children affected; 
 
(c) whether the Government has assessed the nutritional impact of such withdrawal or substitution, 
particularly on underweight, stunting and anaemia among children, if so, the details thereof; 
 
(d) whether the Government has issued guidelines to ensure that school meals are based on scientific 
nutritional standards while respecting local dietary practices and if so, the details thereof; and 
 
(e) whether nutritional equivalence standards have been prescribed for substitutes provided in place 
of eggs under the PM POSHAN Scheme, if so, the details thereof? 
  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (e): Education is part of the Concurrent List of the Constitution and most of the Government 
Schools and School Boards are under the administration of the State Government  and Union 
Territory (UT) Administrations. PM POSHAN Scheme is implemented in partnership with the State 
Governments and UT Administrations. The overall responsibility for providing hot and nutritious 
meal to all children studying in Bal Vatika (just before class 1) and classes I to VIII of Government 
and Government aided schools lies with the State Governments and UT Administrations. The States 
and UTs are encouraged to decide menu suitable to the local conditions within the prescribed 
nutrition and food norms and to procure locally grown food items like millets, vegetables, 
condiments etc.  
 

Under the PM Poshan Scheme, one hot cooked meal is provided to all eligible children on all 
school working days. As per the provisions of National Food Security Act, 2013 and the Guidelines 
of the Scheme, the nutritional and food norms prescribed under the Scheme are as follows: 
 
Items For children of Primary 
classes 
For children of Upper Primary 
classes 
A) Nutritional Norms (Per child per day) 
Calorie 450 700 
Protein 12 gms 20 gms 
B) Quantum of Food Norms (Per child per day) 
Food-grains 100 gms 150 gms 
Pulses 20 gms 30 gms 
Vegetables 50 gms 75 gms 
Oil & fat 5 gms 7.5 gms 
Salt & condiments As per need As per need 
 
Further, there is a provision of 5% of total recurring budget as the flexi component to be used 
by the States/UTs for setting up of School Nutrition Gardens (SNGs) and provision of 
supplementary nutrition interventions in identified districts. Many States/  UTs also provide 
additional supplementary nutrition keeping in view local food habits, cultural preferences, 
availability and dietary practices.  
 
Regarding the impact of PM Poshan Scheme, NITI AAYOG has conducted the evaluation 
of the Scheme through independent third -party agency in 2025 -26. The study concluded that the 
PM POSHAN scheme  has a positive impact on  improving child nutrition and boosting learning 
outcomes.

entries.t: Development of Eco-tourism Trails in Chhattisgarh
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1266 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
Development of Eco-tourism Trails in Chhattisgarh  
 
 
1266. SMT. ROOPKUMARI CHOUDHARY: 
 
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state 
 
(a) whether the Government has formulated any policy for the development of Eco-tourism Trails, if 
so, the details thereof, State/UT-wise including Chhattisgarh; 
(b) the details of Eco-tourism and biodiversity conservation projects sanctioned during the last three 
years in Barnawapara, Sitanadi and Udanti Wildlife Sanctuaries, Kanger Valley National Park, 
Indravati Tiger Reserve, Achanakmar Tiger Reserve and Guru Ghasidas-Tamor Pingla Tiger Reserve, 
along with the funds released; 
(c) whether any Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) has been issued for biodiversity conservation 
and mitigation of human-wildlife conflict in eco-tourism areas; and 
(d) the measures taken to promote tribal participation and generate local employment through eco-
tourism in Barnawapara Wildlife Sanctuary, Sitanadi Wildlife Sanctuary and Udanti Wildlife 
Sanctuary in Chhattisgarh, and whether the Government proposes to further strengthen eco-tourism 
infrastructure in these protected areas? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a)  The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has issued Guidelines for Sustainable 
Ecotourism in Forest and Wildlife Areas-2021. An indicative list of potential eco-tourism areas has 
been annexed to the Guidelines which inter-alia includes sites in Chhattisgarh. 
 
(b)  Ecotourism and biodiversity conservation is primarily the responsibility of the concerned State 
Government and Union Territory Administrations, and are undertaken in accordance with 
prescriptions of an approved Management Plan, Tiger Conservation Plan and Working Plan, as 
applicable. No specific ecotourism project has been sanctioned by the Ministry of Environment, 
Forest and Climate Change for the State of Chhattisgarh. However, financial assistance is provided 
to the State under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats 
for protection, conservation and management of wildlife and development of its habitats. The details 
of funds released to the State of Chhattisgarh under the aforesaid scheme during last three years is as 
below: 
Rs in lakhs 
2023-24 2024-25 2025-26 
409.10 443.57 266.58 
 
 

(c) and (d)  The Ministry has released species-specific guidelines on 21.03.2023 for mitigation of 
Human Wildlife conflicts involving Elephant, Gaur, Leopard, Snake, Crocodile, Rhesus Macaque, 
Wild Pig, Bear, Blue Bull and Blackbuck taking a Harmonious Coexistence Approach for addressing 
human-wildlife conflicts. The Ministry has also issued guidelines for crosscutting issues such as 
cooperation with media, occupational health and safety in human-wildlife conflict mitigation, crowd 
management and addressing health emergencies arising out of human-wildlife conflict situations. 
Moreover, Field Manual for Frontline Staff on Human-Elephant Conflict Management has been 
issued. Further, the National Tiger Conservation Authority hasissued following three SOPs to deal 
with human-animal conflict, which are available in public domain: 
 
i. To deal with emergency arising due to straying of tigers in human dominated landscapes 
ii. To deal with tiger depredation on livestock 
iii. For active management towards rehabilitation of tigers from source areas at the 
landscapelevel. 
 
The three SOPs inter alia include the issue of managing dispersing tigers, managing livestock kills so 
as to reduce conflict as well as relocating tigers from source areas to areas where density of tiger is 
low, so that conflict in rich source areas does not occur. 
 
The National Tiger Conservation Authority has also issued the Normative Standards for Tourism 
Activities and Project Tiger Guidelines, 2012. These guidelines provide for conservation of ecology; 
community participation including tribal communities thereby promoting livelihoods and ensuring 
their stake in such endeavors. 
 
As per information provided by the State Government, several measures have been taken to promote 
tribal participation and generate local employment through eco-tourism. Local youths have been 
selected as guide for tourists. Joint Forest Management Committees (JFMC) have been involved in 
trekking, bird watching, boating and running of canteen. Gypsy vehicles have been provided to JFMC 
from revolving fund for income generation of local people.

entries.head:

Compliance of NGT Orders 
 
1268. SHRI SANJAY UTTAMRAO DESHMUKH: 
 
Will the Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government has the details of the projects received during the last five years 
for Environmental Clearance ; 
(b) if so, the details thereof, region-wise along with their status; 
(c) whether the Government has developed any mechanism to monitor the compliance of the 
orders of the National Green Tribunal; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (b) The Government of India has issued Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) 
Notification, 2006 under the powers conferred by sub-section (1) and clause (v) of sub-section 
(2) of section 3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. As per the provisions laid down in 
the EIA Notification, 2006, as amended from time to time, the proposals specified in its 
Schedule are appraised by the Expert Appraisal Committee (EAC) at Central Level and State 
Expert Appraisal Committee (SEAC) at the State/UT Level, considering all the environmental 
implications associated with the project, including issues raised during the Public Consultation. 
Based on the recommendation of the EAC/SEAC, projects are further considered by the 
Ministry or State Environmental Impact Assessment Authority (SEIAA) at Central Level and 
State/UT level respectively, for approval for grant of Environmental Clearance (EC) or 
otherwise. As per the provisions stated above, ECs are granted after considering environmental 
issues and incorporating appropriate environmental safeguards, including mitigation measures 
prescribed in the Environmental Management Plan (EMP). 
 
As per the extant provisions of the EIA Notification, 2006, as amended from time to time, 
Environmental Clearance is required for project activities falling under the 38 categories 
specified in its Schedule. The state-wise details of proposals granted EC by the Ministry during 
the last five years are placed at Annexure I. 
 
(c) to (d) All directions issued by the Hon'ble Tribunal to the Ministry are followed up for next 
necessary action/compliance by the respective Divisions/Sectors and the Hon'ble Tribunal is 
constantly informed from time to time, wherever required.
