Sports facilities in Aspirational Districts 
 
1336. Adv Gowaal Kagada Padavi: 
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of major schemes being implemented at the national level 
for development of  sports infrastructure and promotion of sports 
facilities in rural and tribal areas across the country; 
 
(b) the details of facili ties provided under these schemes including 
development of  playgrounds, indoor sports infrastructure, training 
centres and coaching support for rural youth; 
 
(c) the number of villages and sports facilities developed under these 
schemes in Nandurbar  district of Maharashtra along with the present 
status thereof; and 
 
(d) the current status of availability, utilisation and maintenance of 
sports infrastructure across  the country, State/UT -wise particularly in 
tribal and aspirational districts? 
 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS  
[ DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA ] 
 
(a) to (d ) ‘Sports’ being a State subject, the responsibility for 
development of sports, including development of sports infrastructure 
and promotion of sports facilities in rural, tribal and aspirational districts 
of the country , rests primarily with the respective State/Union Territory 
Governments. The Union Government supplements these efforts by 
bridging the critical gaps.  The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports 
implements the following scheme s for the promotion of sports in the 
country, including in the State of Maharashtra: 
 
(i)     Khelo India – National Programme for Development of Sports; 
(ii)     Assistance to National Sports Federations (NSFs); 

Page 2 of 2 
 
(iii) Cash Incentives to Medal Winners in International Sports Events 
and their Coaches; 
(iv) National Sports Awards; 
(v)     Pension to Meritorious Sportspersons; 
(vi) Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay National Welfare Program for 
Sportspersons; 
(vii) National Sports Development Fund; 
(viii) Running Sports Training Centres through Sports Authorit y of 
India (SAI); and 
(ix) National Centre for Sports Science and Research (NCSSR). 
 
Details of the above schemes are available in the public domain on the 
websites of this Ministry and the Sports Authority of India. 
 
The Khelo India Scheme and National Sports Development Fund (NSDF), 
implemented by this Ministry, under which financial assistance for 
development of sports infrastructure  is provided are demand -driven 
schemes. The proposals received from the State/ Union Territory 
Governments and other eligible en tities are considered for financial 
support, subject to their completeness, technical feasibility and 
availability of funds under the scheme. The details of the sports 
infrastructure projects approved and their sanctioned cost, funds 
released and their physical and financial progress, under the Khelo India 
Scheme and National Sports Development Funds (NSDF), across the 
country, including in the State of Maharashtra, are available in public 
domain on the dashboards of the Ministry at 
https://mdsd.kheloindia.gov.in and http://www.nsdf.yas.gov.in/nsdf -
glance.html, respectively. 
 
The sports facilities supported under these schemes are available to all  
citizens of the country, including in rural, tribal and aspirational districts. 
The responsibility of operation and maintenance of these sports 
facilities rests with the grantee.

entries.t: Establishment of Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas in Peddapalli and Mancherial
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION & LITERACY 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1338 
ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
Establishment of Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas in Peddapalli and Mancherial 
 
1338. Shri Vamsi Krishna Gaddam: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
 
(a) whether the Government is considering any proposals for Jawahar Navodaya 
Vidyalayas in Peddapalli and Mancherial; 
 
(b) if so, the details of the present status and deficiencies pointed out along with the 
expected approval timeline; 
 
(c) whether the Government is likely to sanction the schools during 2026-27; and 
 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (d): The Navodaya Vidyalaya Scheme envisages for opening of one Navodaya 
Vidyalaya (NV) in each district of the country. Opening of new NVs in uncovered 
districts is a continuous process which depends on the willingness of the concerned 
State Government/UT admi nistration to make available requisite suitable land, free 
of cost, for construction of the permanent building and making available required 
temporary building, free of rent, to run the Vidyalaya till the permanent building is 
constructed. Sanction and ope ning of new NVs depends on approval by the 
competent authority as per extant procedures. Peddapalli and Mancherial districts of 
Telangana do not have NV at present. As on date, 16 NVs have been sanctioned in 
16 districts of Telangana, out of which 15 NVs are functional.

entries.t: Allocation of Funds to Kerala under the 16th Finance Commission
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF EXPENDITURE 
LOK SABHA 
 UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-1340 
ANSWERED ON- 27/07/2026 
 
ALLOCATION OF FUNDS TO KERALA UNDER THE 16th FINANCE COMMISSION  
 
1340. Adv Dean Kuriakose: 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the details of the total funds allocated to the State of Kerala as per the devolution of funds under 
the 16th Finance Commission, year-wise; 
 
(b) the details of the funds actually released to the State of Kerala against the allocated amount 
under the above recommendations, year-wise; and 
 
(c) whether any amount remains pending for release to the State of Kerala under the 16th Finance 
Commission and if so, the details thereof?  
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) and (b): The Union Government vide Explanatory Memorandum as to the Action Taken on the 
Recommendations made by the Sixteenth Finance Commission (16th FC) in its Report for the 
award period 2026-27 to 2030-31 has inter-alia accepted the recommendations for States’ Share 
in Central Taxes and grants-in-aid, viz Local bodies grants and Disaster management grants. 
Accordingly, the recommendations of the 16th FC are being implemented from 1st April, 2026. As 
per the accepted recommendations of the 16th FC, the B.E. 2026-27 for devolution of shareable 
taxes and duties to the State of Kerala is ₹ 36,355.39 crore, of which ₹ 8,869.49 crore has been 
released till 10.07.2026. Releases for the remaining period of the Finance Commission Cycle will 
be made in the respective Financial Year. 
  
 (c): Ministry of Finance, Department of Expenditure releases Central Finance Commission 
recommended grants-in-aid to States on the recommendations of the Nodal Ministries concerned, 
subject to fulfilment of stipulated conditions associated with each component of the recommended 
grants-in-aid. As far as release of FY 2026-27 is concerned, no proposal from the Nodal 
Ministry(ies), is pending for release of grants-in-aid to the State of Kerala.

entries.t: Promoting Sports and Physical Fitness in Gujarat
entries.head:
Page 1 of 2 
 
Government of India 
Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports 
Department of Sports 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1341 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
Promoting Sports and Physical Fitness in Gujarat 
 
1341. Smt. Poonamben Hematbhai Maadam: 
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken initiatives to promote sports and 
physical fitness in Gujarat; 
 
(b) if so, details thereof; 
 
(c) the details of the schemes implemented by the Government for the 
development of sports  infrastructure and youth programmes across the 
country, state/UT-wise; and 
 
(d) the details of the number of sports infrastructure projects sanctioned 
in Gujarat under schemes such as Khelo India? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS  
[ DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA ] 
 
(a) to ( c) ‘Sports’ being a State subject, the responsibility for 
development of sports, including promotion of sports and physical 
fitness and development of sports infrastructure, rests primarily with the 
respective State/Unio n Territory Governments. The Union Government 
supplements their efforts by bridging critical gaps. The Ministry of Youth 
Affairs and Sports implements the following schemes for promotion of 
sports in the country, including in the State of Gujarat: 
 
(i)     Khelo India – National Programme for Development of Sports; 
(ii)     Assistance to National Sports Federations (NSFs); 
(iii) Cash Incentives to Medal Winners in International Sports Events 
and their Coaches; 
(iv) National Sports Awards; 
(v)     Pension to Meritorious Sportspersons; 

Page 2 of 2 
 
(vi) Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay National Welfare Program for 
Sportspersons; 
(vii) National Sports Development Fund; 
(viii) Running Sports Training Centres through Sports Authority of 
India (SAI); and 
(ix) National Centre for Sports Science and Research (NCSSR). 
 
Details of the above schemes are available in the public domain on the 
websites of this Ministry and the Sports Authority of India. 
 
In addition, the “ Fit India Movement ” component of the Khelo India 
Scheme aims to encourage citizens to adopt healthy lifestyles through  
regular physical activity, and promotes fitness awareness at the 
grassroots level via initiatives such as Fit India Week, Fit India Freedom 
Run, Fit India Quiz, and the Fit India Mobile App. The Movement has 
significantly contributed to fostering a culture of health and fitness 
among youth and the wider community across the country , including in 
the State of Gujarat. 
 
Further, the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports implements the following 
schemes to promote youth programmes across the country , including i n 
the States of Gujarat: 
 
(i) Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat); 
(ii) Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan (NYKS); and 
(iii) National Service Scheme (NSS) 
 
(d) The details of the sports infrastructure projects approved and their 
sanctioned cost, funds released and their physical and financial 
progress, under the Khelo India Scheme and National Sports 
Development Funds (NSDF), across the country, including in the State of 
Gujarat, are available in public domain on the dashboards of the Ministry 
at https://mdsd.kheloindia.gov.in and http ://www.nsdf.yas.gov.in/nsdf-
glance.html, respectively.

MINISTRY OF CULTURE

CONSERVATION AND PRESERVATION OF HISTORICAL MONUMENTS AND 
CULTURAL HERITAGE 
 
 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM 
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) 
 
There are total 93 centrally protected monuments under the care and maintenance of 
Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) in the State of Haryana and all are in good state of 
preservation. ASI takes up conservation and preservation work as per the need of the 
monument and availability of resources. There is adequate budget, plans and pace for the 
conservation of centrally protected monuments.   
However, GuzarKhedi and Pandu PindaraDham are not centrally protected monument 
under the jurisdiction of ASI. 
 (b) 
 
 
No survey, preservation and conservation work for GuzarKhedi and Pandu PindaraDham 
have been undertaken by the ASI. 
(c) The details of expenditure incurred on the conservation works of centrally protected 
monuments in Hisar and Sonipat constituencies are attached as Annexure I.  
†1342. Shri Jai Prakash: 
Shri SatpalBrahamchari: 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the fact that there is a lack of adequate budget, plans 
and pace for the conservation, preservation, maintenance, restoration and development of 
ancient mounds, stepwells, forts, temples and other historical and religious heritage 
including GuzarKhedi and other archaeological sites, Pandu PindaraDham in Jind district 
located in the Hisar and SonipatLok Sabha constituencies of Haryana; 
 
(b) whether any survey and preservation and conservation work for these heritage sites have 
been undertaken by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), the Ministry of Culture or 
any other competent agencies and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) the details of the funds approved/sanctioned and utilised for the conservation, restoration 
and tourism development of historical monuments and heritage in the said constituencies, 
during the last three years; 
 
(d) whether any new plan proposed by the Government to preserve these heritage sites and 
develop them on the national tourism map as well as cultural heritage; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof along with expected timeline and the anticipated benefits? 

(d) 
& 
(e) 
The development of tourism infrastructure at tourist destinations, including heritage cities, 
is primarily undertaken by the concerned State Governments or Union Territory 
Administrations. However, the Ministry of Tourism, under its “Pilgrimage Rejuvenation 
and Spiritual, Heritage Augmentation Drive” (PRASHAD) Scheme, provides financial 
assistance to State Governments (SGs) and Union Territory Administrations (UTAs) for 
the development of tourism-related infrastructure at identified religious and heritage sites 
across the country, including the State of Haryana. 
The Ministry of Tourism has sanctioned 1 project "Development of Mata Mansa Devi 
Temple and Nada SahebGurudwara in Panchkula District" at the cost of Rs. 48.53 Crore.

entries.t: Funds for Simhastha Kumbh Mela
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF TOURISM 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION No.1343 
ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
FUNDS FOR SIMHASTHA KUMBH MELA 
 
1343. SHRI BHASKAR MURLIDHAR BHAGARE: 
 
Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the details of the total amount of financial assistance sanctioned by 
the Government for the preparations and organization of the 
forthcoming Simhastha Kumbh Mela at Nashik, component-wise; 
(b)  the details of the funds released so far, phase and purpose-wise; 
(c)  whether the Government has constituted any High-Level Committee, 
Steering Committee or Monitoring Committee to oversee the 
planning, implementation and utilization of Central assistance for the 
Simhastha Kumbh Mela, and if so, the details thereof; 
(d)  the composition of the said Committee, including the names and 
designations of its members and whether the Member of Parliament 
representing the Nashik Lok Sabha Constituency has been included 
therein; and 
(e) the details of the measures taken by the Government to ensure 
transparency, timely execution of projects and effective coordination 
among all stakeholders for the successful conduct of the Simhastha 
Kumbh Mela? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM         (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (e):  Ministry of Tourism sanctions Central Financial Assistance for 
the promotion of fairs and festivals to the State Governments, including 
Maharashtra and Union Territory (UT) Administrations, subject to receipt 
of proposals and adherence to the Scheme Guide lines. No proposal has 
been received from the Government of Maharashtra in the Ministry for the 
forthcoming Simhastha Kumbh Mela at Nashik.  
  
The State Government of Maharashtra has informed that a 
comprehensive Kumbh Mela Development Plan amounting to Rs 22,425.39 

crore has been approved by the Hon`ble Chief Minister of Maharashtra in 
the meeting of the Apex Committee, held on 13.3.2026. The Government 
of Maharashtra, has constituted a 40 member Apex Committee under the 
Chairmanship of the Hon`ble Chief Minister, an Executive Committee for 
planning, co-ordination and organization of the Mela and a Kumbh Mela 
Ministers` Committee to take policy decisions. It has been informed by the 
State Government that the Member of Parliament representing the Nashik 
Lok Sabha Constituency have been included in the Apex Committee.  
 
The State Government has established the Nashik -Trimbakeshwar 
Simhastha Kumbh Mela Authority for inter -departmental co -ordination,  
project planning, fund management and effective execution of 
development works for the forthcoming Mela.

entries.t: Employment Status in Sidhi Lok Sabha Constituency
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1344 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27TH JULY, 2026 
 
EMPLOYMENT STATUS IN SIDHI LOK SABHA CONSTITUENCY 
 
1344.      DR. RAJESH MISHRA : 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the status of youth unemployment in the Singrauli district of Madhya 
Pradesh despite the presence of heavy coal mining and power plants; 
(b) the total number of youth got employment through the District 
Employment got Exchange and the National Career Service Portal in 
Sidhi and Singrauli districts during the last three years; and 
(c) whether the Government proposes to launch any special skill 
development scheme or establish technical training centre to train the 
youth in Sidhi Lok Sabha constituency in accordance with the demand 
of local heavy industries Northern Coalfields Limited (NCL) and National 
Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC), Adani and Hindustan Aluminium 
Corporation (HINDALCO)? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) to (c): Official estimates of employment and unemployment in India are 
derived from the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), conducted by the 
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation since 2017 –18. The PLFS 
methodology was revamped with effect from January 2025. The PLFS Annual 
Report 2025 is the first report in the revised series to present labour market 
estimates, covering the period from January to December 2025. 
As per latest PLFS report 2025, the estimated Unemployment Rate (UR) 
for youth of age 15 -29 years was 4.2% in 2025 in the State of Madhya Pradesh 
(including the Singrauli district). Further, the estimated Worker Population 
Ratio (WPR) indicating employment on usual status for youth of age 15-29 years 
and above was 51.6% in the State of Madhya Pradesh (including the Singrauli 
district) compared to 41.4% in the country in 2025. 
Further, more than 8.23 crore (of which 18.60 lakh in the State of 
Madhya Pradesh) net subscribers have joined Employees’ Provident Fund 
Organization (EPFO) between September 2017 and July 2025 indicating 
increase in employment and formalization of the job market. Also, more than 
1.29 crore (of which 2.84 lakh in the State of Madhya Pradesh)  net subscribers 
have joined EPFO during the year 2024-25. 

The NCS Portal brings together Jobseekers and employers on one 
platform to facilitate job opportunities and career related services to the 
Jobseekers of the country. Further, notifying final hiring figures is not a 
mandatory requirement on NCS portal. However, the job hiring data is available 
only to the extent as voluntarily reported by the employers. 
 
Employment generation coupled with improving employability is a 
priority of the Government. Accordingly, Government is implementing various 
employment generation schemes/ programmes in the country (including the 
Singrauli district of Madhya Pradesh). The details of various employment 
generation schemes/ programmes being implemented by the Government may 
be seen at   https://dge.gov.in/dge/schemes_programmes. 
 
Government is also implementing Skill India Mission (SIM) to deliver 
skill, re -skill and up -skill training through an extensive network of skill 
development centres/ schools/ colleges /institutes etc. under various schemes, 
viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan 
(JSS), National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsmen 
Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in the 
country (including the Singrauli district of Madhya Pradesh). The SIM aims at 
enabling youth of India to get future ready, equipped with industry relevant 
skills. 
 
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has 
initiated ‘FutureSkills PRIME’ a programme for Re -skilling/Up-skilling of IT 
Manpower for Employability in 10 new/emerging technologies including 
Artificial Intelligence. 
 
 
Additionally, the Government is implementing Employment Linked 
Incentive (ELI) Scheme named as the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar 
Yojana to support employment generation, enhance employability and social 
security across all sectors, with special focus on the manufacturing sector. 
The scheme with an outlay of Rs 99,446 Crore aims to incentivize the creation 
of more than 3.5 Crore jobs in the country, over a period of 2 years. 
Further, Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India, is 
running the National Career Service (NCS) Portal which is a one -stop solution 
for providing career related services including jobs from private and 
government sectors, information on online & offline job fairs, job search & 
matching, career counselling, vocational guidance, information on skill 
development courses, skill/training programmes etc. through a digital platform 
[www.ncs.gov.in]. 
 
*****

entries.t: Wage Ceiling Limit for ESI Coverage
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1345 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
WAGE CEILING LIMIT FOR ESI COVERAGE 
 
1345. SHRI N K PREMACHANDRAN: 
 
         Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)whether the Government proposes to increase the wage ceiling 
limit for Employees' State  Insurance (ESI) coverage and if so, the 
details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(b)whether the Government is aware that the wages of the 
workers/employees are increased due to the increase of their living 
cost; 
(c)if so, the reasons for the ESI wage ceiling limit not increasing 
corresponding to the said increase; 
(d) whether the Government proposes to extend the ESI coverage to 
more sectors and if so,  the details thereof and if not, the reasons 
therefor; 
(e)whether the Government proposes to relax the attendance, 
restrictions imposed for Super  Specialty treatment of seasonal 
workers including cashew workers; and 
(f)if so, the details thereof and action taken thereon? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (f): The revision of wage ceiling is undertaken periodically 
from time to time. The last revision in the wage ceiling for coverage 
under the Employees’ State Insurance (ESI) Scheme was done w.e.f. 
01.01.2017, wherein the wage limit was raised from Rs. 15,000/ - per 
month to Rs. 21,000/ - per month (Rs. 25,000/ - for Persons with 
disability). 
  Employees’ Sate Insurance Act, 1948 has now been 
subsumed in Code on Social Security, 2020 which has been 
implemented w.e.f. 21.11.2025. Under Section 2(29) of the Code on 
Social   Security, 2020, an "establishment"   broadly  covers   places 
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
where industrial, commercial or other specified economic activities 
are carried on. It includes factories, motor transport undertakings, 
newspaper establishments, audio -visual production units, 
construction establishments, plantations, m ines, ports and areas 
where dock work is undertaken. Moreover, Section 45 of the Code on 
Social Security, 2020 empowers the Central Government to frame the 
Scheme for providing the benefits of the ESIC to the Unorganised 
workers, gig workers and platform workers. 
  At present, there is no such provision under ESIC to relax 
the attendance, restrictions imposed for Super Specialty treatment 
of Seasonal factory workers being outside the coverage of ESIC.

entries.t: Cultural Tourism through Heritage Villages
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1346 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
CULTURAL TOURISM THROUGH HERITAGE VILLAGES 
 
1346. SHRI DHARAMBIR SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government proposes to develop Heritage Villages across the country by 
integrating local history, traditional crafts, folk music, cuisine and rural tourism; 
(b) whether any guidelines have been prepared for identifying villages having significant 
historical and cultural importance; 
(c) the details of the incentives proposed to be provided for preservation of heritage structures 
and promotion of local artisans under the scheme; and 
(d) whether any village in the Bhiwani-Mahendragarh Lok Sabha Constituency has been 
identified or proposed to be identified under the said initiative? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF CULTURE & TOURISM 
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (d): The Ministry of Culture is not implementing any specific scheme for the development of 
Heritage Villages through the integration of local history, traditional crafts, folk music, cuisine, 
and rural tourism.However, the Ministry of Culture undertakes activities relating to the research, 
documentation, preservation, and dissemination of India's tangible and intangible cultural heritage. 
It also documents and digitally maps the cultural heritage of villages across the country, including 
local history, traditional crafts, folk traditions, art forms, and other cultural assets. Such 
documentation and cultural mapping initiatives may provide academic and archival support to 
broader heritage development programmes undertaken by the Government. 
 
*****

entries.t: Expansion and Modernization of the ITI Ecosystem
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1348 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27TH JULY, 2026 
 
EXPANSION AND MODERNIZATION OF THE ITI ECOSYSTEM 
 
1348.      SHRI RAJPALSINH MAHENDRASINH JADAV: 
 
Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has increased the number and capacity 
of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in the country; 
(b) the details of expansion undertaken since the year 2014 till now 
along with details for the training capacity at present; 
(c) the salient features of the 'Upgraded ITI through Pradhan Mantri 
Kaushal and Rozgar Parivartan (PM -SETU)' scheme, including the 
hub-and-spoke model and investment outlay thereof; and 
(d) the steps taken for the modernization of Government ITIs along 
with Introducing future ready trades as per the requirements of 
industry? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
 
(a) & (b): The number of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) across the 
country has increased from 9,642 in 2014 to 13,856 in 2026 and the 
Seating capacity in these ITIs have increased from 17,42,986 in the 
Session 2014-15 to 20,07,580 as on date. The State -wise number of ITIs 
(in Year 2014 and in Year 2026) and their seating capacity is at 
Annexure -I. 
  
(c) & (d): The Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation 
through Upgraded ITIs (PM -SETU) scheme aims to enhance the overall 
quality and relevance of vocational training in the country. The Scheme 
has a total outlay of Rs. 60,000 crore (Central Share – Rs. 30,000 crore, 
State Share – Rs. 20,000 crore and Industry Share – Rs. 10,000 crore). 
  
 
 

The scheme comprises of two components: 
  
(i)    Component I – Upgradation of 1,000 Government ITIs (200 Hub ITIs 
and 800 Spoke ITIs) in a Hub and Spoke model wherein upgradation 
includes smart classrooms, modern labs, digital content, and new 
courses aligned to industry needs. 
  
(ii)     Component II – Capacity Augmentation of five NSTIs located in 
Bhubaneswar, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kanpur, and Ludhiana, including 
setting-up sector -specific National Centres of Excellence for skilling, 
with focus on advanced training of trainers with global partnership, and 
curriculum development.  
 
As per the Cabinet approval, the selection of ITIs under PM SETU 
scheme is led by the respective State/ Union Territory (UT) Governments 
in consultation with industry, ensuring alignment with emerging skill 
needs and local industrial potential. Accordingly, States/ UTs 
Government submits their proposals for upgradation in collaboration 
with industry partners. 
  
Further, under the PM -SETU scheme industry -led Special Purpose 
Vehicles (SPVs) lead the upgradation and are empowered to propose 
necessary interventions relating to curriculum redesign in mining, 
manufacturing and other sectors, training delivery models, infrastructure 
upgradation and industry exposure, in alignment with local industry 
needs and the Scheme guidelines. Directorate General of Training (DGT) 
has introduced 32 new age courses under CTS. List of these new age 
courses are given in Annexure - II.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1349 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY, JULY 27, 2026/SHRAVANA 5, 1948 (SAKA) 
 
UTILISATION OF CSR FUNDS IN UTTAR PRADESH 
QUESTION 
 
†1349. Shri Neeraj Maurya: 
 
Will the Minister of CORPORATE AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware that companies are required to spend their 
Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds in the local areas under Section 
135(5) of the Companies Act, 2013 but units like Indian Farmers Fertiliser 
Cooperative Limited (IFFC O) located in Aonla in Uttar Pradesh violate this 
provision by utilising the CSR funds outside the local area, if so, the details 
thereof; 
 
(b) the details of the total funds allocated and the actual expenditure incurred on 
local healthcare, education, and environmental initiatives by the major corporate 
units operating in the districts of Bareilly, Budaun and Shahjahanpur in Uttar 
Pradesh during the last three years, unit wise; 
 
(c) whether the Government proposes to ensure punitive action and special 
compliance audit against companies found not spending funds in accordance 
with the prescribed rules in the districts of Bareilly, Budaun and Shahjahanpur, if 
so, the details thereof; and 
 
(d) whether the Government proposes to direct such companies to set up 
multidisciplinary skill development centres for local youth through the CSR funds 
within a specified time-limit and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CORPORATE AFFAIRS   AND MINISTER 
OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
[SHRI HARSH MALHOTRA] 
(a):    Under the Companies Act 2013, CSR is a Board driven process and the Board 
of the company is empowered to plan, decide, execute and monitor CSR activities 
of the company based on the recommendation of its CSR Committee. This 
Committee formulates and recomme nds the CSR policy, which outlines the 
activities to be undertaken by the company in alignment with the areas or 
subjects specified in Schedule VII of the Act.  
Contd…2/- 

-2- 
The first proviso to Section 135 (5) of the Act provides that the company  shall 
give preference to the local area and areas around it where it operates.  However, 
the emphasis on local area is only directory and not mandatory in nature. The 
Government does not issue any direction to the companies to spend in any 
particular geographical area or for any particular activity.   
 
(b): There is no provision of allocation of funds in CSR legal framework.  Based 
on the annual filings made by companies in the MCA21 registry, Development 
sector-wise CSR expenditure in the districts of Bareilly, Budaun and 
Shahjahanpur of Uttar Pradesh for the last three Financial Years (FYs) i.e 2022 -
23 to 2024-25 is attached at Annexure-I, II and III respectively.  
 
(c): The CSR Policy implemented by the company has to be disclosed by the 
company in its Board report and the Board has to satisfy itself that the funds so 
disbursed have been utilised for the purposes and in the manner as approved by 
it, and the Chief Financial Officer or the person responsible for financial 
management shall certify to the effect. Further, those companies who have their 
websites are required to make disclosures such as composition of CSR 
Committee, CSR Policy and CSR projects approved by B oard on their website.  
Whenever violation of CSR provisions is reported, action against such non -
compliant Companies is initiated as per provisions of the Act after due 
examination of records and following due process of law.  
 
(d):  There is no such proposal.

entries.t: Relief to Borrowers in Times of Natural Calamities
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF FINANCIAL SERVICES 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO- 1350 
 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY, 27 JULY, 2026/SHRAVANA 5, 1948 (SAKA) 
Relief to Borrowers in Times of Natural Calamities 
†1350. SMT. KRISHNA DEVI SHIVSHANKAR PATEL: 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:- 
(a) the details of the relief provisions made available by banks to borrowers in the event of  
natural calamities; 
(b) whether damage caused by fire incidents is also classified as a natural calamity, if so, the  
details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether it is a fact that banks deny timely relief to their borrowers, leading to a  
deterioration of the financial condition of such borrowers, if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government proposes to provide alternative assistance to borrowers in cases  
where banks fail to extend relief during natural calamities; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
(a): Banks have Board approved policies on relief measures for areas affected by Natural 
Calamities which is guided by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) “Master Directions on Relief 
Measures by Banks in Areas affected by Natural Calamities, 2018” and “Master Directions on 
Resolution of Stressed Assets, 2025” as updated and amended from time to time, the latest 
being the amendments dated 29.4.2026. 
The relief measures are extended on implementation of a resolution plan, taking into 
consideration factors including the decisions of the State Level Bankers' Committee 
(SLBC)/Union Territory Level Bankers' Committee (UTLBC)/District Consultative 
Committee (DCC). Based on the nature and extent of damage, the resolution plan may include 
the following: 
1. Restructuring: This may include extension of loan tenure, conversion of short -term loan 
into long term loan, conversion of unpaid interest into a Funded Interest Term Loan 
(FITL), etc. 
2. Deferment of Equated Monthly Instalment (EMI), 
3. Moratorium, 
4. Rescheduling of Term loans 
5. Additional finance to address the financial stress of the borrower. 

(b): Damage caused by fire incidents is not ordinarily classified as a natural calamity unless it 
forms part of a larger notified disaster event or is specifically recognized/declared by the 
competent authority. In such exceptional cases, relief measures are considered on a case -to-case 
basis as per extant RBI policies and relief measures are extended on the recommendations of 
the SLBC/UTLBC/DCC. 
(c): As per the inputs received from Public Sector Banks, there are no cases reported where the 
eligible borrowers affected by natural calamities have been denied timely relief. The identified 
eligible borrowers are extended the prescribed relief measures, such as 
restructuring/rescheduling of loans, moratorium and other permissible reliefs, as applicable, 
within the timelines stipulated under RBI guidelines and the Bank’s policy. These measures are 
intended to mitigate financial stress and prevent accounts from slipping into Non -Performing 
Assets on account of disruption caused by natural calamities. 
(d) and (e): As per the RBI -Resolution of Stressed Assets, Second Amendment Directions, 
2026 effective from 01.07.2026, the resolution plan for providing relief to affected borrowers is 
required to be invoked no later than  45 days from the date of declaration of the calamity and 
implemented within 135 days from the date of such declaration. 
Further, as per National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM), the primary responsibility 
for disaster management, including disbursal of relief assistance on ground level, rests with the 
State Governments concerned. The State Governments undertake relief measures in the wake 
of natural calamities, from the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) already placed at their 
disposal, in accordance with Government of India approved items and norms. The Central 
Government supplements the efforts of the State Governments and provides requisite logistics 
and financial support. The National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) also supplements SDRF 
of a state, in case of a disaster of severe nature. 
*****

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF CULTURE 
LOK SABHA

ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
LIMIT OF 100-METER CONSTRUCTION RESTRICTION AREA IN CHANDRAPUR 
 
 
†1351. SMT. DHANORKAR PRATIBHA 
SURESH: 
 
Will the Minister of CULTURE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has any plan under consideration to reduce the limit of the 
currently applicable 100-meter construction prohibition zone to 30 meters, in view of the     
extremely dense population in the historical 'Parkota' (fort wall) premises of Chandrapur 
(Maharashtra); 
(b) whether the Government is aware that due to this restrictive/onerous condition, it has 
become difficult for the local citizens to repair their houses and avail the benefits of the 
'Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana' and if so, the details of remedial measures being planned in 
this regard; and 
(c) the details of the steps taken/being taken by the Government to provide special relaxation 
for Chandrapur city in the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 
in order to strike a balance between the conservation of historical heritage and the 
fundamental rights of the local citizens? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF CULTURE AND TOURISM 
(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) At present, there is no such proposal to reduce the existing 100-metre Prohibited Area to 30 
metres in respect of the historical 'Parkota' (fort wall) at Chandrapur, Maharashtra, under 
consideration. 
(b) Under the provisions of the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains 
Act, 1958 (AMASR Act) repair or renovation of eligible existing buildings in the 
Prohibited Area and construction, reconstruction, repair or renovation in the Regulated 
Area are permitted with the prior permission of the Competent Authority, in accordance 
with the provisions of the AMASR Act and the Rules made there under. Applications are 
considered on a case-to-case basis while ensuring the protection and preservation of 
protected monuments and sites (areas) of national importance. 
(c) The AMASR Act does not envisage any separate provision for granting special relaxation 
to any city.  
 
*****

DEVELOPMENT OF HAMPI

 Will the Minister of TOURISM be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has any new plan to develop  Hampi in 
Karnataka as a world-class heritage and tourist destination;  
(b) if so, the details thereof along with the estimated funds and the timeline 
for their implementation;  
(c) whether any proposal relating to Hampi is under consideration under the 
Swadesh Darshan Scheme, the PRASHAD Scheme or any other Central 
tourism scheme and if so, the details thereof; and  
(d) the detail of the steps taken by the Government to improve tourism 
infrastructure and visitors facilities in Hampi, along with the details of 
funds sanctioned and released thereon? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF TOURISM  (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT) 
 
(a) to (d): Identification and development of tourist destinations and tourism 
products is primarily undertaken by the concerned State Governments 
(SG)/Union Territory Administrations (UTA). However, the Ministry of Tourism 
through its schemes of ‘Swadesh Darshan (SD) ’, ‘Swadesh Darshan 2.0 
(SD2.0)’, ‘Challenge Based Destination Development (CBDD)’ – a sub-scheme of 
SD2.0, and ‘Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual, Heritage Augmentation 
Drive (PRASHAD)’ complements the efforts of tourism infrastructure 
development by extending financial assistance to the concerned SG/UTA; 
subject to adherence to scheme guidelines, submission of Detailed Project 
Reports (DPRs) by them, availability of funds, Government directions, inter -se 
priority etc.  
 

Under the Swadesh Darshan 2.0 Scheme, Ministry of Tourism has already 
sanctioned a project for “ setting up of 'Traveller Nooks” at Hampi  in 2023-24 
for ₹25.64 crore and ₹2.56 crore has been authorized for utilization. The project 
envisages enhancement of tourism experience at Hampi. Swadesh Darshan 
scheme is appraised till September, 2026.

entries.t: Restructured PMKVY 4.0
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1356 
ANSWERED ON – 27/07/2026 
 
RESTRUCTURED PMKVY 4.0 
 
1356. DR. LATA WANKHEDE:  
           SMT. SHAMBHAVI: 
 
 Will the Minister of SKILL DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has restructured the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana 
(PMKVY) 4.0 to link central funding of training partners directly to final verified job placements of 
candidates; 
 
(b) if so, the percentage of certified youth from ordinary backgrounds who successfully secured 
regular monthly wage employment within three months of course completion in 2025 -26, 
particularly in Sagar Lok Sabha constituency; 
 
(c) the average starting monthly salary received by rural certified candidates in the retail, 
logistics and healthcare sectors; 
 
(d) whether any digital monitoring platform is operational to track the long -term job retention 
and career growth of these skilled youth; and 
 
(e) the steps taken/being taken by the Government to penalize fraudulent training institutes that 
issue fake certificates without providing actual practical industrial workshop training? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP 
 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (c) Under Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), placements were tracked in 
the Short -Term Training (STT) component in the first three versions of the Scheme which is 
PMKVY 1.0, PMKVY 2.0 and PMKVY 3.0 implemented from FY 2015 -16 to FY 2021 -22. Under 
PMKVY 4.0 which is under implementation since FY 202 2-23, the focus is to empower trained 
candidates to choose their varied career path and they are suitably oriented for the same through 
On-Job Training (OJT) embedded industry relevant skill courses. 
 
(d) MSDE has launched Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH), a unified platform that integrates skilling, 
education, employment, and entrepreneurship ecosystem to provide a lifelong array of services to 
the beneficiaries. Under PMKVY 4.0, post-certification tracking of candidates for one year through 
the SIDH has been provisioned.   
 
(e) To strengthen transparency, accountability, and quality assurance under PMKVY 4.0, the 
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) has put in place a robust monitoring 
and compliance framework. This includes post -certification tracking of can didates, call -based 
validation, technology-driven interventions such as the Facial Authentication Attendance System 
(FAAS) and a real-time attendance dashboard on the SIDH platform, along with structured virtual 
and physical inspections of Training Centres . The Ministry has also revamped the monitoring 
guidelines by introducing well -defined Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), automated risk alerts, 
and a strengthened penalty framework to facilitate timely identification and redressal of non -
compliance. 

 
Based on findings from inspections and verification of records, appropriate enforcement action has 
been taken against non -compliant Training Partners and Training Centres. Such actions include 
issuance of show cause notices, suspension of operations, withholding and recovery of payments, 
cancellation of accreditation and affiliation, blacklisting, and initiation of legal proceedings, 
wherever warranted. As on date , 42 First Information Reports (FIRs)  have been registered, 182 
non-compliant Training Partners/Training Centres  have been blacklisted, and recovery 
proceedings have been initiated to recover financial losses from the defaulting entities.

entries.t: Forest Conservation in Tribal-Dominated Areas
entries.head:
OIH 
           GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
         MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE 
 
      LOK SABHA 
     UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1357 
      TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
        Forest Conservation in Tribal-Dominated Areas 
 
1357. DR. FAGGAN SINGH KULASTE: 
 
  Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government is aware of the fact that human-wildlife conflict, forest degradation and 
climate change are adversely affecting the livelihoods of tribal communities in Madhya Pradesh, 
Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and other tribal-dominated States; 
(b) if so, the State-wise details thereof; 
(c) whether the Government has implemented any special scheme for forest conservation, bio-
diversity enhancement, compensatory afforestation and mitigation of human-wildlife conflict in such 
areas; 
(d) whether the participation of Gram Sabhas and local tribal communities has been ensured in the 
implementation of these schemes; 
(e) whether the Government proposes to implement any new action plan to strengthen the livelihood 
of local communities and environmental security along with forest conservation in tribal-dominated 
areas; and 
  (f) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND 
CLIMATE CHANGE  
(SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH) 
 
(a) to (f)  To enhance the resilience of tribal communities and safeguard their livelihoods, the Ministry 
of Environment, Forest and Climate Change is implementing various schemes such as Integrated 
Development of Wildlife Habitats, MISHTI (Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible 
Incomes), Nagar Van Yojana, and Compensatory Afforestation Fund.  
 
In addition Ministry is also implementing the Green India Mission (GIM) which aims to protect, 
restore, and enhance forest and tree cover while contributing to climate change mitigation and 
adaptation through plantation and ecosystem restoration in identified landscapes. 
 
These schemes are implemented by the respective States/UTs in accordance with the approved 
management plan/ tiger conservation plan/ working plan as applicable which are prepared in 
consultation with Gram Sabhas. 
Under various afforestation programmes, Joint Forest Management Committees (JFMCs) and Eco 
Development Committees (EDCs) are constituted at the village levels, which enables community 
participation in sustainable forest management and wildlife conservation, while addressing the 
livelihood needs of local communities. However, no new scheme is proposed for launch to strengthen 

the livelihood of local communities and environmental security along with forest conservation in tribal 
dominated areas. 
 
Further, for wildlife conservation including the management of human-wildlife conflict, the Ministry 
provides financial assistance to State Governments and Union Territory Administrations under the 
Centrally Sponsored Schemes ‘Development of Wildlife Habitats’ and ‘Project Tiger and Elephant’ 
for management of wildlife and its habitat in the country. The activities supported include procurement 
of early warning systems, construction and erection of physical barriers such as barbed wire fence, 
solar, powered electric fence, bio-fencing, boundary walls etc. as per stakeholder consultation to 
prevent the entry of wild animals into crop fields, compensation for depredation by wild animals 
including cattle lifting, crop damage, loss of life and property. Rapid Response Teams are also 
deployed to mitigate Human-Wildlife Conflict.

entries.t: Assessment of India's Fiscal and Inflation Outlook
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF ECONOMIC AFFAIRS 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1359 
TO BE ANSWERED ON MONDAY, JULY 27, 2026 
 
Assessment of India's Fiscal and Inflation Outlook 
 
1359. Prof. Sougata Ray: 
        Shri Kishori Lal: 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has assessed the impact of easing international crude oil prices and 
improving global supply chains on India's fiscal and inflation outlook; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether any revision in fiscal projections is under consideration, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) the steps being taken by the Government to safeguard the economy against external geopolitical 
uncertainties? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (c): The global economic situation has been volatile in the last five months. The international 
crude oil prices (Brent) have moderated from the peak USD 138.2 per barrel reached in April 2026 to 
a low of USD 68.5 per barrel in July 2026 and currently stand at around USD 87.0 per barrel as on 20 
July 2026. As per Federal Reserve Bank of New York, the Global Supply Chain Pressure Index has 
declined from 1.84 in April 2026 to 1.25 in June 2026, reflecting an impr ovement in global supply 
chain conditions. The moderation in crude oil prices and easing of global supply chain pressures are 
expected to reduce imported inflationary pressures, moderate input and logistics costs, and support 
India's fiscal and inflation o utlook. The Reserve Bank of India has projected Consumer Price Index 
(CPI) inflation at 5.1 per cent for 2026 -27, while noting that the inflation outlook remains subject to 
upside risks from global commodity price movements and supply chain disruptions. On the fiscal front, 
the Government remains committed to the budgeted fiscal deficit target of 4.3 per cent of GDP for 
2026-27. However, the Government continues to closely monitor evolving global developments and 
their implications for the Indian economy, a nd take appropriate policy measures, as warranted, to 
safeguard macroeconomic stability. 
  

(d) The Government has adopted a comprehensive and multi -pronged approach to safeguard the 
economy against external geopolitical uncertainties. Energy security has b een strengthened through 
diverse strategies such as diversification of crude oil import sources, expansion of strategic 
partnerships, augmentation of Strategic Petroleum Reserves, promotion of alternative fuels, domestic 
production of critical energy input s, and implementation of Coal and Lignite Gasification Scheme. 
Demand-side initiatives, such as encouraging LPG consumers to shift to PNG, have also been 
undertaken to optimise energy use. To support trade and industry, measures such as the RELIEF 
(Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation) Scheme, Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool, 
restoration of RoDTEP (Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products) benefits, faster customs 
clearances, logistics facilitation, targeted customs duty relief and the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee 
Scheme (ECLGS) 5.0 have been introduced.  In addition, the Government is strengthening trade 
resilience by expanding its network of Free Trade Agreements and Comprehensive Economic 
Partnership/Cooperation Agreements. 
The Government has also ensured adequate availability of fertilisers and other essential agricultural 
inputs through assured gas supplies, diversification of import sources, advance procurement and 
maintenance of buffer stocks. These efforts are complem ented by initiatives of the Reserve Bank of 
India to strengthen external  sector resilience and support foreign exchange inflows through 
liberalisation of the External Commercial Borrowing (ECB) framework, measures to facilitate foreign 
investment, special swap facilities and promotion of local currency settlement with partner countries. 
Together, these coordinated measures strengthen India's macroeconomic stability and reduce the 
economy's vulnerability to external shocks.

entries.t: Decline in Indian Students Pursuing Higher Education in Canada
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1360 
ANSWERED ON 27/07/2026 
 
Decline in Indian Students Pursuing Higher Education in Canada 
 
1360. Shri Haribhai Patel: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
a) whether the Government has taken note of the reported decline in the number of Indian 
students opting for Canada for higher education during 2026, if so, the details thereof along 
with the principal academic, immigration, financial and other factors influencing this 
changing trend; 
b) the initiatives proposed by the Government to strengthen academic programmes, 
international collaborations, research infrastructure, innovation ecosystems and faculty 
exchange in higher education al institutions to provide globally competitive lea rning 
opportunities within the country; 
c) the manner in which Indian Missions abroad disseminate authentic and updated guidance 
on admission procedures, visa norms, living expenses, student welfare and emplo yment 
prospects in major study destinations; 
d) the details of the assistance and advisory support extended by the Government to Indian 
students affected by changes in immigration, visa or post -study work policies in foreign 
countries; and 
e) whether the Government has established any framework to monitor developments in the 
international education and issue timely guidance enabling prospective Indian students to 
make informed decisions regarding overseas higher education and if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) Studies abroad is a matter of individual will and choice, which is contingent on a variety of 
factors, including affordability, access to bank loans, exposure to foreign societies, aptitude for 
particular branch of studies.  
 

As per inputs received from Ministry of External Affairs, t he decline in the number of Indian 
students opting for Canada for higher education d uring 2026 is primarily attributable to changes 
in Canada's international student policies  which includes cap on new international study permits 
which is being progressively reduced year on year. Principal factors influencing this trend include: 
 
 Immigration policies 
 Increase in proof of funds requirement to a minimum of CAD 22,895 per year for 
Indian students 
 Narrowing of eligibility for Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) by Government 
of Canada. 
 
(b) The Government of India has undertaken several  initiatives to ensure availability of high -
quality education in the higher education , including through infrastructure upgradation of public 
funded educational institutions, accreditation of new institutions and courses  which meet the 
criteria under National Accreditation Board, promotion of research & innovation and augmenting 
digital initiatives for accessibility. These initiatives have contributed to the increasing quality of 
educational facilities in the country. As a result, 52 Indian Institutions are now in the QS World 
University Ranking (QS WUR) 2027 with 13 Indian universities securing a place among the 
Global Top 550, which is India’s highest ever representation, marking an increase from 11 Indian 
institutions in QS WUR 2015.  As per Global Innovation Index (2025)  India is ranked 38th 
globally. India is considered to be one of the largest startup ecosystems in the world (top 3) in 
scale, funding and unicorn count.  
 
In order to provide the best of global educational facilities within the country and in line with the 
vision of National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 to promote internationalization of education and 
making India a global hub for higher education, Foreign Higher Educational Institutions (FHEIs) 
have been permitted to establish their campuses in India under: 
 the (UGC) University Grants Commission (Setting up and Operation of Campuses 
of Foreign Higher Educational Institutions in India) Regulations 2023, and  
 the International Financial Services Centers Authority (Setting up and Operation of 
International Branch Campuses and Offshore Education Centers) Regulations, 
2022.  
 
UGC has issued 16 Letters of Intent (LoIs) to 15 FHEIs from Australia, Italy, United Kingdom 
and USA to establish their campuses at various places in India including Bengaluru, Greater Noida, 
Gurugram, Mumbai and Chennai. Under IFSCA regulations, 2022, approvals have been granted 
to five universities from Australia and the UK to establish offshore branch campuses in GIFT City, 
Gandhinagar, Gujarat.  
 
Further, University Grants Commission (UGC) has taken several initiatives to enhance quality of 
education, including financial support to HEIs. Some of the important initiatives  of UGC include 

issuing regulations for  Joint/Dual/Twinning degree programmes, guidelines for 
Internship/Apprenticeship Embedded Degree Program , establishment of  Research and 
Development Cells in HEI

entries.t: Establishment of New Kendriya Vidyalayas and PM-SHRI Schools in Maharashtra
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF SCHOOL EDUCATION AND LITERACY 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1361 
ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
Establishment of New Kendriya Vidyalayas  
and PM-SHRI Schools in Maharashtra 
 
†1361. Shri Omprakash Bhupalsinh Alias Pavan Rajenimbalkar: 
 Shri Sanjay Uttamrao Deshmukh: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether the Government has received proposals from Maharashtra and other 
States for the establishment of new Kendriya Vidyalayas (KVs) and PM School 
for Rising India (PM-SHRI) Schools; 
(b)  if so, the number of such proposals received, district -wise and the present 
status of the said proposals, along with the timeline for their approval and 
implementation; 
(c)  the total number of  Kendriya Vidyalayas and PM -SHRI Schools presently 
functioning in the State of Maharashtra; 
(d)  whether the proposal made by Public Representative for setting up Kendriya 
Vidyalayas and PM-SHRI schools in Dharashiv district has been considered by 
the Government, if so, the present status thereof; 
(e)  whether there exists a demand-supply gap in access to quality CBSE-affiliated 
Kendriya Vidyalayas in the rural and semi -urban areas of Maharashtra, if so, 
the details thereof; 
(f)  whether the Government has identified any new locations or educationally 
backward districts in Maharashtra including Dharashiv for the establishment of 
new Kendriya Vidyalayas or PM-SHRI Schools; and 
(g)  if so, the details thereof with specific reference to the Washim -Yavatmal 
Parliamentary Constituency? 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(SHRI JAYANT CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) to (g) Opening of new Kendriya Vidyalayas (KVs) is a continuous process. KVs are 
opened primarily to cater to the educational needs of the wards of transferable Central 
Government Employees including Defence & Para -military personnel, Central 
Autonomous Bodies, Central Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) and Central Institute 

of Higher Learning (IHL) by providing a common programme of education throughout 
the country. Proposals for opening of new KVs may be sponsored by Ministries or 
Departments of the Government of India / State Governments / Union Territories (UTs) 
Administrations, with commitment to provide requisite resources including land and 
temporary accommodation for setting up a new KV as per norms.  The proposals are 
subject to approval of the competent authority as per extant procedures. KVs are not 
opened on the criteria of rural/urban/backward districts/aspirational district/State/UT 
etc.  
At present, 63 KVs are functional in the State of Maharashtra including 02 KVs 
in Washim-Yavatmal Parliamentary Constituency i.e. PM SHRI KV, Washim and KV , 
Yavatmal. All KVs are affiliated to CBSE by providing a common programme of 
education throughout the country.  
As per information received from Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan (KVS), no 
feasible proposals, as per norms of KVS, for opening of new KVs have been received 
by KVS from State Government of Maharashtra/District Administrations.  
The proposals received from the sponsoring authorities for opening of new KVs 
are examined / processed at various levels and are required to be considered in a 
holistic manner in accordance with the extant guidelines, inter alia taking into account 
various factors including the availability of resources and overall feasibility. 
Pradhan Mantri Schools for Rising India (PM SHRI) is a centrally sponsored 
scheme which aims to strengthen more than 14,500 schools from amongst the existing 
schools managed by Central Government/State/UT Government/local bodies.  
  
Under PM SHRI scheme, the selection of PM SHRI schools is done through the 
Challenge Mode, wherein schools compete for support to become exemplar schools. 
The criteria adopted by the Government for selecting the schools under the PM SHRI 
scheme are provided under “Selection Met hodology” of the PM SHRI Framework, 
available at the link: https://pmshri.education.gov.in/assets/pdf/part1_pmshri.pdf.  
 
Under PM SHRI scheme, a total of 946 schools including 52 KVs have been 
selected from the State of Maharashtra . The details of PM SHRI schools may be 
accessed on the website of PM SHRI scheme at the link: 
https://pmshri.education.gov.in/state.  
*****

entries.t: Benefits of Social Security Schemes in Uttar Pradesh
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1362 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
BENEFITS OF SOCIAL SECURITY SCHEMES IN UTTAR PRADESH 
 
†1362. SHRI RAMASHANKAR VIDHARTHI RAJBHAR: 
 
         Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a) the details of the number of workers who have been registered on 
the e-shram portal provided benefits under various social security 
schemes in Uttar Pradesh, district and occupation-wise; 
(b) the details of the percentage of the said workers who could not 
receive benefits under social security schemes due to delay in the 
disbursement of benefits during the last three years; 
(c) the details of the number of workers who are associated with the 
power loom industry  registered on the e -shram portal in Uttar 
Pradesh, district-wise; and 
(d) the steps taken by the Government to increase the registration of 
workers engaged in the  handloom, handicrafts and Powerloom 
sectors on the e -shram portal and  ensure their wider  coverage 
under various social security schemes?  
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (d): The Ministry of Labour and Employment launched eShram 
portal (eshram.gov.in) on 26 th  August, 2021 for creation of a 
comprehensive National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW). 
The eShram portal registers the unorganised workers and provides 
them a Universal Account Number (UAN) on a self-declaration basis. 
  District-wise and occupation sector -wise details of 
unorganised workers registered on the eShram portal in the State of 
Uttar Pradesh are at annexure- I and II respectively.  
  Details of unorganised workers in the State of Uttar 
Pradesh registered on the eShram portal enrolled under various 
social security schemes is at annexure-III. 
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
  Ministry of Labour and Employment launched the eShram–
“One-Stop-Solution” o n 21 st October 2024. eShram – “One-Stop-
Solution” entails integration of different social security/ welfare 
schemes at single portal i.e. eShram. This enables unorganised 
workers registered on eShram to access social security schemes and 
see benefits availed by them so far, through eShram. 
  District-wise details of unorganised workers associated 
with the powerloom industry registered on the eShram portal in 
State of Uttar Pradesh are at annexure -IV. 
 
  To enhance registrations under the eShram  initiative and 
ensure wider coverage of unorganised workers including in the 
handloom, handicrafts and Powerloom sectors, the Government has 
adopted a comprehensive strategy. In addition to enabling self -
registration through the web portal and mobile appl ication, assisted 
registration modes have been introduced via Common Service 
Centres (CSCs), State Seva Kendras (SSKs), and the UMANG platform 
to facilitate easy access for workers. The Ministry of Labour and 
Employment is conducting targeted awareness cam paigns 
comprising registration drives, community outreach programs and 
locally tailored communication efforts. To strengthen outreach, the 
Ministry leverages social media channels to disseminate videos, 
tutorials, and other informative content, making the initiative more 
accessible and engaging. 
 
  To further enhance the availability and accessibility of 
eShram and its associated services to unorganised workers, the 
Ministry of Labour and Employment officially launched the eShram 
mobile application on 24th February 2025. This application facilitates 
real-time access to welfare schemes integrated with the eShram 
platform, thereby significantly strengthening both accessibility and 
user convenience.

entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1363 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
MEDICAL FACILITIES FOR TRIBAL WORKERS 
 
†1363. SHRI MANSUKHBHAI DHANJIBHAI VASAVA: 
 
         Will the Minister of LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)the details of medical facilities being provided by the Government 
to the tribal workers across the Country, State/UT-wise; 
(b)the details of hospitals and healthcare institutions establi shed in 
tribal-dominated areas  along with the sanctioned strength and 
working strength of doctors, Paramedical staff and other personnel 
in each of the said hospitals/healthcare institutions; 
(c)the details of the medical equipments and devices available f or 
various tests, diagnostic facilities and other allied services in the 
said hospitals/healthcare institutions; and 
(d)the plans being formulated by the Government to bring reforms in 
the conditions of the said hospitals/healthcare institutions? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT 
(SUSHRI SHOBHA KARANDLAJE) 
(a) to (d): Public health and hospitals are State subjects. 
Accordingly, the primary responsibility for planning, establishing, 
maintaining, and ensuring an adequate number of healthcare 
facilities rests with the respective State Governments. Under the 
National Health Mission (NHM), the Government of India provides 
financial and technical assistance to States/UTs for strengthening 
their healthcare systems based on the proposals received in their 
Programme Implementation Plans, within the approved resource 
envelope. 
  Health Dynamics of India (HDI) (Infrastructure & Human 
Resources), 2023 –24 is an annual publication based on healthcare 
administrative data reported by States/UTs. S tate/UT-wise details 
regarding the availability of healthcare facilities, specialized human 
resources, and gaps, including those in remote, hilly, and tribal areas, 
are available at the following link: 
Contd..2/- 

:: 2 :: 
https://www.mohfw-
dohfw.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/05/57202cf30629539e4d0fb0a2f70
0ac62.pdf 
  Under Ayushman Bharat, 1.86 lakh Ayushman Arogya 
Mandirs (AAMs), including 31,366 AAMs across 178 tribal districts, 
provide comprehensive primary healthcare by strengthening Sub 
Health Centres (SHCs ) and Primary Health Centres (PHCs). These 
AAMs deliver preventive, promotive, rehabilitative, and curative 
healthcare services covering reproductive and child healthcare, 
communicable and non -communicable diseases, and other health 
conditions. The State -wise number of operational AAMs in tribal -
dominated areas is at Annexure. 
  Teleconsultation services are available at all operational 
AAMs across the country, enabling access to specialist healthcare 
closer to people's homes and addressing issues related t o physical 
accessibility, shortage of healthcare providers, and continuity of 
care. As on 30.06.2026, a total of 46.90 crore teleconsultations have 
been conducted through AAMs across the country. 
  Mobile Medical Units (MMUs) provide primary healthcare 
services to remote, tribal, and underserved populations, including 
OBC, SC, and ST communities. As per NHM MIS (December 2025), a 
total of 1,546 MMUs are operational across the country in such areas. 
  Under the Free Drugs and Free Diagnostics Service 
Initiative, the Government of India provides financial support to 
States/UTs for the provision of 113 drugs and 14 diagnostic tests at 
SHC-AAMs, 179 drugs and 63 tests at PHC -AAMs, 301 drugs and 97 
tests at Community Health Centres (CHCs), 318 drugs and 111 tests  
at Sub -District Hospitals (SDHs), and 381 drugs and 134 tests at 
District Hospitals (DHs). 
  The Government has taken several measures to 
strengthen healthcare services, including implementation of the 
Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-
ABHIM) and support through the recommendations of the Fifteenth 
Finance Commission for strengthening health infrastructure.

entries.t: Disinvestment and Asset Monetisation
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF INVESTMENT AND PUBLIC ASSET MANAGEMENT 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1364 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON MONDAY , JULY 27, 2026/SHRAVANA 5, 
1948 (SAKA) 
 
Disinvestment and Asset Monetisation 
 
1364. Com. Selvaraj V: 
          Shri Subbarayan K: 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Government has raised about Rs. 25,000 crore 
from disinvestment and asset monetisation so far in the current fiscal; and 
 
(b)  if so, the details of the public sector companies from which this money is 
raised and the proposed timeline for achieving the target of Rs. 80,000 crore 
envisaged in the FY 27 budget? 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) & (b):  During the current FY 2026-27, Government of India realized an 
amount of Rs. 26,639.33 core as on 22.07.2027, which included Rs 20,272.40 
crore from disinvestment through Offer for Sale of Central Bank of India, Coal 
India Ltd, NHPC Limited, NLC India Limited, General Insurance Corporation of 
India, Indian Railway Finance Corporation Ltd. and Cochin Shipyard Ltd and 
Rs. 6,366.93 crore from Asset Monetization. 
 
Fixing separate disinvestment targets has been discontinued since FY 2023-
24. However, Rs. 80,000 crore has been kept under Miscellaneous Capital 
Receipts for BE 2026-27, which includes estimated receipts on account of 
management of equity investments and public assets through various 
mechanisms.   Disinvestment is an ongoing process and execution/completion 
of specific transactions hinges upon market conditions, domestic and global 
economic outlook, geopolitical factors, investor interest and administrative 
feasibility. Further, given the market-sensitive nature of disinvestment 
transactions, drawing up timeline for disinvestment is not feasible.

entries.t: Unutilization of National Sports Development Fund (NSDF)
entries.head:
Page 1 of 2 
 
Government of India 
Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports 
Department of Sports 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1365 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.07.2026 
 
Unutilization of National Sports Development Fund (NSDF) 
 
1365. Smt. Sajda Ahmed: 
 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has taken note of concerns regarding under-
utilisation and  improper utilisation of funds under the National Sports 
Development Fund (NSDF); 
 
(b) the details of allocation and actual utilisa tion of NSDF funds during 
the last five years and the current year, year-wise; 
 
(c) whether regular audits of the Fund are being conducted and if so, the 
details and findings thereof; and 
 
(d) the corrective measures taken by the Government to ensure 
transparency, accountability and effective utilisation of NSDF funds ? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS & SPORTS  
[ DR. MANSUKH MANDAVIYA ] 
 
(a) to (d) The National Sports Development Fund (NSDF), established in 
1998 under the Charitable Endowments Act, 18 90, aims to promote 
sporting excellence by supporting elite athletes, facilitating 
international training and exposure, organising national and international 
sporting events, and developing sports infrastructure. It complements 
flagship schemes like Khelo India by providing need -based financial 
assistance for high -performance sports and infrastructure, including a 
block grant to the T arget Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) for Olympic 
and Paralympic medal preparation. 
 

Page 2 of 2 
 
NSDF operates under a robust institutional and financial governance 
framework. Proposals are appraised as per approved guidelines, 
considered by the Executive Committee (EC),  and ratified by the NSDF 
Council. Funds are released in a milestone -linked, phased manner, with 
subsequent instalments conti ngent upon submission and verification of 
Utilisation Certificates. Physical progress of infrastructure projects is 
monitored throu gh periodic reports, including geo -tagged photographs, 
ensuring timely and eligible utilisation of funds. 
 
On the audit front , NSDF accounts are prepared annually in formats 
prescribed by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India and 
audited yearly by a Chartered Accountant appointed with EC approval. 
The audited annual accounts are then submitted to t he CAG for review,  
following which the CAG issues a draft Separate Audit Report (SAR). 
NSDF's reply to any findings/observations in the draft SAR is submitted 
for consideration, leading to finalisation of the SAR by the CAG. 
 
Together, this appraisal, approval, mon itoring, and audit mechanism 
ensures that NSDF assistance is extended only for eligible activities and 
effectively contributes to the development of sports and sportspersons 
in the country. 
 
NSDF receives contributions through Corporate Social Responsibility 
(CSR) contributions from Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs), corporate 
houses and voluntary donations from individuals, which are matched by 
a 25% c ontribution from the Government. The details of rece ipts,

entries.t: Stand up India Scheme in Mumbai
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
DEPARTMENT OF FINANCIAL SERVICES 
 
LOK SABHA  
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 1366 
ANSWERED ON MONDAY, 27 JULY, 2026/SHRAVANA 5, 1948 (SAKA) 
Stand up India Scheme in Mumbai 
 
1366.  PROF. VARSHA EKNATH GAIKWAD: 
 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state:  
 
(a)  whether the Government has reviewed the implementation of the Stand -Up India Scheme in  
Mumbai, Maharashtra, if so, the details and key findings thereof; 
 
(b) the number of Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and women entrepreneurs in Mumbai who have 
availed loans ranging from 10 lakh to 1 crore under the Scheme during the last three years and the 
current year; 
(c)  whether eligible beneficiaries in Mumbai are being provided margin money support of upto 25 
percent of the project cost through convergence with eligible Central and State Government the 
schemes, if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether the Government is aware of difficulties faced by SC/ST and women entrepreneurs in 
Mumbai in obtaining timely loan sanct ions, collateral -related assistance, mentoring and 
handholding support under the Scheme, if so, the details thereof and the corrective steps taken 
thereon? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI PANKAJ CHAUDHARY) 
 
(a) No specific study for the implementation of the Stand-Up India Scheme in Mumbai, Maharashtra 
has been conducted.  
However, an independent impact assessment study for Stand Up India Scheme at national level was 
undertaken during FY 2019-20. 
Further, the evaluation of the Scheme was conducted through DMEO, NITI Aayog during FY 2024-
25. Few of the key findings of evaluation are as under: 
i. Study found Stand Up India Scheme to be largely aligned with the Sustainable Development 
Goals (SDGs) and the National Policy for Women. 
ii. Stand Up India Scheme businesses across sectors have generated an employment of around 4 
to 12 employees on an average. 
iii. Stand Up India Scheme loans helped entrepreneurs in improving their financial conditions and 
reduced reliance on informal credit by improving cash flow and increased revenue. 
 

 
(b) The number of Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and Women entrepreneurs in Mumbai who have 
availed loans ranging from Rs.10.00 lakh to Rs.1.00 crore under the Scheme during last three years 
(April, 2023 till March, 2025) is as under:

Scheduled Tribe (ST)      18 
Women (incl.SC/ST)

Total* 1,485 
 
*The Scheme was operational till March, 2025 for sanctions. 
(c) Scheme allows for convergence of project cost upto 15% with other eligible central and state 
government Schemes. Data for such convergence details is not maintained centrally. 
(d) To mitigate the difficulties faced by SC/ST/Women entrepreneurs, the Governm ent has taken 
various steps towards effective implementation of the existing Schemes.  These, inter alia, include 
intensive publicity campaigns, simplification of application form, Credit Guarantee Scheme, 
reduction in borrower’s own contribution, inclusio n of activities allied to agriculture and frequent 
reviews at various level to monitor the achievement against allocated target etc.  
 Apart from linking prospective borrowers with banks for loans, the online portal 
(www.standupmitra.in) for Stand-Up India Scheme provided guidance to prospective entrepreneurs 
in their endeavour to set up  business enterprises, starting from training to filling up  of loan 
applications as per Bank requirements.  
   The Jan Samarth portal acts as a one-stop digital platform for linking various Government-sponsored 
loan schemes, including Stand Up India Scheme (SUPI), thereby facilitating easy access for 
applicants under the loan Schemes.
